title: Manager, Building Maintenance and Operations
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Purpose
The Manager, Building Maintenance & Operations (“Manager”) is responsible for the first‑line management of the building, and provides coordination and planning throughout the Law Society. This includes the planning, implementation and monitoring of safe and efficient services related to mechanical and electrical maintenance and operations and overseeing various service contracts.
 
The Manager is also accountable for the effective management of employees to facilitate responsive support services to employees across the organization. This includes managing the day-to-day work order management, janitorial services, move management, and ergonomic requests. 
 
Qualifications

The minimum level of education required is a post-secondary university and/or college diploma or equivalent, with courses in general mechanical and electrical services, health and safety, fire and building codes. 
Professional Engineer, LEED AP, and/or IFMA designations with facilities management experience implementing / managing BOMA certification program(s) is desirable.
As the Manager is expected to provide hands‑on management, the incumbent is required to have a minimum of 7 years of broad experience with a strong mechanical aptitude and experience, with at least 2 years of supervisory experience in a customer service-oriented environment.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

Thorough knowledge of mechanical systems and its associated distribution including, but not limited to, low pressure steam (ENWAVE) and circulating hot water heating systems and forced air heating and cooling systems, their maintenance and operation. 
Thorough knowledge of electrical systems and its associated distribution including high voltage sub stations, electrical rooms with associated equipment, etc.
Thorough knowledge of plumbing systems and its associated distribution including sewage sump pits, boilers, tanks, etc.
Thorough knowledge of fire alarm systems and its associated distribution including F/A panels, sprinkler systems, heat/smoke detectors, etc. 
Proven mechanical ability in assessing and scheduling repairs and service calls for various equipment. 
Ability to read floor plans and technical drawings (i.e., riser diagrams, schematics, details, etc.) along with excellent reading and writing skills.
Thorough knowledge of construction/building materials and their usages.
Working knowledge of industry standards and safety guidelines, WHMIS, OHS Act, AODA, Building Codes, Fire Codes, Electrical Codes.
Good computer skills, experience in the use of Microsoft Word, Excel, and G Suite (Gmail, Calendar, etc.).
Sustainability: Identify and implement initiatives, cost savings, energy reduction and efficiencies with current and new equipment, systems, operations, etc.
Working knowledge of a Computer Maintenance Management System (Asset Essentials)
Working knowledge of Building Automation Systems (Automated Logic).
Speaks and writes in a clear, articulate manner for individual and/or group situations.
Valid driver’s license is desirable.

Technical Skills and Knowledge

Familiarity with various software applications, including word processing, spreadsheets and computer assistance drawing programs, e‑mail and the Intranet/Internet.

Key Accountabilities
 
Client / Customer Service Planning

Plans and coordinates the service delivery of the Building Maintenance and Operations team to ensure the safe, clean, and efficient operation of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, pneumatic and electronic systems. 
Collects, monitors, and evaluates utility and waste consumption data to help implement opportunities for operational cost savings, reduce utility consumption, and improve operational efficiencies of building engineering systems.
Implements and manages a nationally recognized facility operations certification program to help continuously track and assess building operational efficiency, improve sustainability practices, reduce overall environmental footprint, and lower carbon generation.  
Evaluates the required maintenance or operational work to be completed within the building and based on the impacted variables (building operations, department operations, costs/budget, time/scheduling, and physical site constraints/logistics), strategically develops a plan which minimizes negative impacts to LSO operations, while considering costs.
Evaluates the health and safety risks (dust, odours, noise, fire, flood, etc.) associated with proposed maintenance work, and details the appropriate health and safety measures to ensure both regulatory compliance while addressing any work specific concerns.  
Oversees various service contracts, including but not limited to, groundskeeping, waste management, office cleaning, office shredding, graffiti removal, elevator maintenance, building automation system maintenance, emergency power testing and maintenance, grease trap removal, backflow prevention inspections, fire safety systems, washroom and hygiene products.  
In collaboration with the Director, Facilities and Planning and department representatives, assesses the impact of programs related to mechanical and electrical systems, staffing, maintenance projects, budgets, supplies, and legal issues, recommending courses of action.  
Plans for potential utility outages and troubleshoots to determine faults, and initiate repairs of infrastructure systems.  
Coordinates and supervises preventative and proactive maintenance and repairs of systems. 
Receives requests for services from staff throughout the building, assessing feasibility and prioritizing maintenance requests, liaising with clients to ensure that needed support is provided in a timely and efficient manner.  
Completes work requests, either directing employees, and/or coordinating with external contractors.   
Prepares Requests for Proposals, interviews, and decides on successful contractors, seeking input and approval from the Director for major contracts.

 Client / Customer Service Delivery

Actively contributes to the secure and safe maintenance, repair and replacement of mechanical and electrical systems. 
Responds to employee, member and builder users’ related issues and concerns.  

Monitors contracts and service contractors for compliance with scope, timeline, budget and quality control, and effectiveness of service delivery.
Establishes relationships with service providers to maintain service level agreements beneficial to the Law Society.  

Identifies and implements initiatives for cost savings, energy reduction and improved efficiencies with current and new equipment, systems, and operations, with a commitment to sustainability.
Performs daily monitoring and checks, anticipating deadlines and seasonal requirements.  
Monitors and maintains inventories of supplies, including required purchasing.  
Keeps accurate and timely logs and schedules.  
Ensures all services meet relevant codes and standards, including health and safety, WHMIS, and regular inspections, such as fire monitoring and sprinkler systems.  
Maintains current knowledge and expertise in the area of mechanical services, ensuring a proactive approach to service delivery. 
Resolves escalated issues related to consultant, supplier, and/or service contracts.

 People Leadership

Hires, develops, and assesses performance of team members in accordance with the policies of the organization and best human resources practices.  
Fosters a team environment by clarifying team goals, valuing team input, building team member commitment, strengthening the team’s collective skills and encouraging creativity and problem solving.  
Provides input into departmental issues resolution, vision, and communication strategy.
Ensures career development of direct reports by coaching, training and/or mentoring; conducts performance reviews for direct reports within the department.
Supervises day-to-day activities of team performing technical work and ensures quality standards and procedures are followed and met.
Provides direction and checks the quality of contractors’ and service providers’ work, negotiating contracts and ensuring cost‑effectiveness and conformance with legal requirements.

 Financial Responsibility

Oversees the preparation of contract services, quotations from external vendors, and manages team through the execution of each contract. 
Tracks and reports on utility and contract services expenditures, negotiates contracts with clients and vendors, to ensure cost effective utilization of resources.
Responsible for annual expenditure, revenues, and contract negotiations related to external building maintenance service providers.
Analyzes budget needs and contributes to the development of the Maintenance and Operations budget process, including forecasts for materials purchases and replacements, services and staffing.  
Monitors the appropriate budget, taking corrective action on variances.  
Receives requests for supplies and equipment, conducting purchases within approved budget and guidelines, meeting cost‑effectiveness requirements, and ensuring adequate stock of inventories.  
Provides support to the Director and assists in budgeting and budget monitoring.

 Team Membership

In conjunction with the Director and other team members, contributes to the proactive planning of immediate and longer term departmental, opportunities and initiatives, and works with the team to implement cost-effective, user-friendly solutions. 
Coordinates and communicates with the immediate team, employees, internal and external clients, consultant, vendors, and contractors throughout planning and execution of maintenance work.

title: Bookkeeper, Regulatory Services (Hybrid)
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Purpose
 
The Bookkeeper is responsible for the exploration and resolution of financial matters that arise from formal Trusteeships and informal arrangements with licensees. This includes: a review of licensee books and records, reconciliation of the trust accounts where feasible, drafting reports to counsel summarizing the review and reconciliation, reviewing client files, and determining entitlement to trust funds and processing the distribution of trust funds held.
 
Qualifications

Minimum of 5 years’ accounting or bookkeeping experience in a law office or legal environment
Familiarity with law firm billing and bookkeeping software, and specifically, PC Law, is required
Experience reconciling law practice accounts, maintaining client trust ledgers is required. A broad exposure to various types of client matters is desirable.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:

Solid understanding of the Law Society’s rules, legislation and by-laws relating to law firm accounting 

Solid understanding of the Law Society’s mandate, services, legislation, and policies 

 
Previous experience in a legal environment

Concise, well organized writing skills in the preparation of reports and allocation of funds
Strong analytical skills
Ability to multitask efficiently with a great attention to detail

Technical Skills and Knowledge:

Computer literacy, including word processing software, advanced spreadsheet functions and accounting system software  
High proficiency in PC Law required. Experience with other law firm computer programs is desirable                                    

Key Accountabilities:
 
Client / Customer Service Delivery
 

Reviews licensee books and records, financial documents, and client files to reconcile trust accounts and determine proper client ledger allocations and distributions, where feasible.
Liaises with financial institutions to request and receive trust funds and financial documentation. 
Liaises with trust claimants, beneficiaries, and others, as necessary. 
Reports on activities to Counsel with carriage of the file and/or to the Team Managers as directed and administers distribution of funds held in trust to persons beneficially entitled. 
Provides assistance and support to the Officer responsible for bookkeeping activities and maintenance of the Unclaimed Trust Fund.
May provide affidavit evidence and/or oral testimony or submissions related to trusteeship matters and/or other matters pertaining to the functioning of the Law Society. 
May assist licensees, their family members, estate trustees, assisting colleagues and/or successor licensees on financial matters relating to practice windup. 
May attend on practice recoveries to assist with the general recovery of a practice and/or with the recovery of financial documents, data, and digital devices. 

 
Policy / Regulatory Compliance
 

Examines accounting and bookkeeping records and files maintained by licensees, identifying, and advising counsel of apparent deficiencies, discrepancies, and shortfalls. 
Helps to facilitate the identification, recovery and cataloguing of financial records related to a licensee’s professional business. 
Assists Counsel in the preparation of court materials, provides affidavit evidence and/or testifies as a witness, as required. 
Assists Officer with bookkeeping activities and maintenance of the Unclaimed Trust Fund.

 
Performance Goals, Targets and Standards
 

Contributes to the development of standardized practices, guidelines, and procedures in the administration of Trusteeships from an accounting and bookkeeping perspective. 
Maintains own caseload, and works with other members of the Trustee Services department, particularly Counsel and Officers, to establish, monitor and continuously improve processes and case management performance targets.

 
Policy Development
                                    

Assesses policies and procedures, and proactively identifies opportunities for policy development or change in areas related to trusteeships and related activities. 
Participates in the development of policy and procedures when assigned.

 
Team Membership
                                                                        

Works closely with Trustee Services staff in the administration of Trusteeships informal practice wind-up matters, and the Unclaimed Trust Fund, including: responding to inquiries and requests for funds, attending at practice recoveries, and in assisting with other functions on as-needed basis. 
Promotes the sharing and transfer of knowledge and information amongst team members.

title: Representative, Membership Services
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Purpose
Delivers timely, accurate, and high-quality client service to licensees, internal departments, and external stakeholders by supporting a range of financial and administrative functions (e.g., fee adjustments, status changes, certificates of standing, LSO portal support, processing Law Society ID Cards, diploma replacements, etc.). Handles financial transactions on behalf of licensees, such as invoice adjustments and assists with credits to licensees’ accounts. Responds to inquiries related to continuing professional development (CPD) requirements and membership services, and provides guidance to paralegals regarding professional liability insurance.
Qualifications

Requires completion of a 2-year college program in Business, Accounting, or a related discipline.
Requires a minimum of 2 years of experience providing client service in a high-volume call centre, preferably in the financial services industry.
Professional knowledge:

Superior customer service, particularly related to financial services.
Knowledge of the Law Society, including organizational structure, services, mandate, by laws, rules and regulations.
Knowledge of other legal resources and agencies (e.g., Legal Aid, LawPRO, Law Foundation, etc.) and their relation to the LSO and the Membership Services function.
General accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and internal controls.

Technical skills:

Microsoft Office Suite / 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
LSO’s CRM platform, Ozzie (MS Dynamics).
Microsoft SharePoint.

Competencies:

Customer service skills.
Analytical and problem-solving skills.
Interpersonal, oral, written, and presentation skills. Clear, concise, and articulate verbal and written communication skills to compose correspondence, convey detailed information, and provide explanations in an audience-appropriate format.
Organizational and multitasking skills with attention to detail.
Mathematical acumen.

Key Accountabilities
Client / Customer Service Delivery

Provides a range of membership services, including billing, status changes, and certificates of standing, in accordance with Client Service Centre (CSC) and Law Society standards for timeliness, accuracy, and quality.
Liaises with internal departments and external agencies to verify and reconcile member information, ensuring that the member database remains current and accurate, including updates to status and financial records.
Contributes to the achievement of individual service targets related to accuracy, timeliness, and quality of service delivery.

Financial Responsibility

Processes financial transactions related to fee-for-service member offerings, such as Law Society ID cards and certificates, and handles payments (cash, credit, debit) for reinstatements from administrative suspensions and other fee-related services.
Ensures the accuracy of all financial transactions and compliance with internal controls and departmental accounting procedures.

Team Membership

Collaborates with other Representatives to exchange information, share expertise, and provide support to ensure accurate, timely, and high-quality service delivery.
Demonstrates flexibility and strong team orientation by assisting colleagues and maximizing resources during peak periods (e.g., suspensions, bar admissions).
Actively participates in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance work processes, procedures, and service delivery, supporting optimal individual and team performance.

title: Legal Assistant, Litigation Services (Contract)
description:
Job Purpose
 
Provides legal administrative support to the department, including the Director, Senior Manager, Senior Team of Litigators and Discipline Litigators. Plans, organizes, and coordinates practices and procedures support, ensuring ongoing case management while meeting competing deadlines relating to the internal complaints process and regulatory and/or court proceedings. Prepares hearing documentation for Tribunal and court proceedings, providing para-professional, organizational, and technical support while maintaining strict confidentiality.
 
Qualifications
 

Requires completion of a 2-year college program in Law Clerk or Paralegal diploma or a related discipline.
Requires either Law Clerk Certificate and membership in the Institute of Law Clerks of Ontario, a Paralegal license, or a license with the Law Society, or equivalent experience (at least 5 years of significant and directly relevant experience).
Requires a minimum of 5 years’ experience as a law clerk or legal assistant in a law practice, government, and/or regulatory environment (preferably litigation).
Professional Knowledge:

Solid knowledge of law office, court, and/or tribunal practices and procedures is essential, including legal terminology; the drafting, preparation and handling of legal correspondence and documents (affidavits, legal correspondence, etc.)
Working knowledge of the Rules of Civil Procedure and/or the applicable Rules of Practice for an Administrative Tribunal.
Knowledge of the Law Society’s organizational structure, services, mandate, rules, and regulations is an advantage or willingness to learn.
Knowledge of current trends and developments in the legal profession.
Knowledge of legal procedures and substantive areas of law (e.g., real estate, estates, and family law.)
Written and verbal skills in French would be an asset.

Technical Skills: 

Microsoft Office Suite / 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
Case management systems and software such as Adobe Acrobat DC, ShareFile, SharePoint.
Experience locating legal cases on CanLII.
Conducting internet directory searches, and research on a variety of legal and internet searches.

Competencies: 

Customer service skills
Analytical and problem-solving skills
Relationship Management
Interpersonal, oral, and written communication, and presentation skills
Organizational and multitasking skills with attention to detail
Project coordination, prioritization, and time management skills
The ability to work independently and as a team member in a fast-paced environment while balancing competing priorities and deadlines.
Excellent attention to detail and proofreading skills.

 
Key Accountabilities
 
Case Management and Legal Document Handling:

Assists and ensures procedural, legal, and administrative requirements are met with respect to applications before the Tribunal and Courts, including file management, document preparation, correspondence, service of documents, and liaising with witnesses.
Prepares and files materials for hearings, motions, and appeals with the Tribunal Office and Courts, ensuring compliance with the Law Society’s Rules of Practice and Procedure and the Rules of Civil Procedure.
Prepares affidavits, charts, correspondence, and memoranda, and organizes legal materials, including books of authorities, document books, facta, exhibits, and hearing briefs for the Discipline Litigator’s review.
Coordinates the service of materials to relevant parties through process servers, and emails, ensures accurate and timely maintenance of the case management system.
Orders transcripts from court reporters and court offices.
Contacts court offices to obtain documents or information concerning ongoing investigations, regulatory proceedings and/or appeals from regulatory proceedings, as required.
Redacts confidential information from documents for filing at hearing.
Reviews reports to ensure the case management system is up to date.
Reviews investigation documents for disclosure, organizes, finalize and redact documents for Discipline Litigator’s review.

 
Client Service, Scheduling, and Hearing Coordination:

Maintains and monitors calendars of case related deadlines for Discipline Litigators. 

Monitors deadlines and due dates for case preparation.
Interacts with staff, licensees, applicants, witnesses and complainants regarding sensitive, privileged and/or high-profile matters. 
Responds to queries while meeting customer service standards.
Assists Discipline Litigators with witness interviews, including notetaking, and collecting documentation. 
Prepares summonses to witnesses, coordinates with witnesses regarding availability, and arranges travel or virtual hearing appearances.
Scheduling of appointments and meetings, ensuring room setup, required documentation, attendee availability, and interpreter services.
May be required to testify at regulatory proceedings, including undergoing cross-examination by defense counsel. 

 
Financial Responsibility: 

Maintains and orders office supplies for assigned work area. 
Ensures the efficient operation of all office equipment.
Prepares expense reports, cheque requisitions, and processes invoices for payment.

 
Team Collaboration and Process Improvement:

Engages in problem-solving with other team members to continuously improve workflow and departmental effectiveness.
Identifies and addresses gaps in work processes, making recommendations for workflow and efficiency improvements to optimize both individual and departmental performance.
Promotes the sharing and transfer of knowledge and expertise amongst other team members.
Assists staff in using computerized support systems effectively to enhance productivity.
Monitors legal topics and file management trends, forwarding relevant issues to staff to support policy development and process improvements.
Supports departmental projects and initiatives aimed at enhancing operational efficiency.

title: Counsel, Licensing Equity Initiatives, Licensing and Accreditation
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Summary 
Counsel, Licensing Equity Initiatives supports the Law Society’s licensing and accreditation mandate with a focus on equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) and Indigenous issues, applying an EDI and Indigenous lens to licensing policies, processes, and practices. The role serves as a direct, proactive support to licensing candidates – particularly Indigenous candidates and others from equity-deserving groups – by navigating complex licensing requirements, addressing barriers, managing escalations, and resolving sensitive or high-impact files. Acts as a trusted internal legal resource for licensing and accreditation with strong cultural competence and equity-informed practice, contributing to the consistent and equitable development, interpretation and application of licensing standards, content and policies. Works collaboratively with colleagues and internal and external stakeholders on program design and delivery to strengthen relationships with Indigenous communities and equity-deserving interest groups across Ontario. Contributes to research, guidance materials, and training initiatives that support inclusive practices within the Licensing and Accreditation department.
 
Qualifications

Requires an LLB or JD.
Requires a Class L1 licence with the Law Society of Ontario.

Requires a minimum of 5 years’ experience either practising law or working in the area of legal professional development. 

Requires demonstrated experience working with EDI and/or Indigenous issues. 

Experience in a professional body, government, post-secondary education institution, or in a legal practice is preferred.
Professional Knowledge:

Designing, delivering, and evaluating defensible licensing systems and processes.
Law Society’s mandate, services, rules, and regulations.
Program design processes, publication production, and principles and best practices for adult learning and instructional methodologies.
Entry-level competencies for licensees.
Equity and access to justice related legislation, theory, and practice, including employment and human rights legislation, jurisprudence, and best practices.
Research and analytical tools and methods.
Solid understanding of Indigenous affairs, culture, and communities and the relationship between the Law Society and the Indigenous community.

Technical Skills: 

Microsoft Office Suite / 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
Distance learning and/or assessment technologies are an asset.

Competencies:

Customer service skills.
Negotiation skills with tact and diplomacy.
Analytical and problem-solving skills.
Project coordination, prioritization, and time management skills.
Interpersonal, oral, and written communication, and presentation skills.
Organizational and multitasking skills with attention to detail.
Relationship Management.
Research skills.
Legal writing skills.

 
Key Accountabilities
 
Client / Customer Service Delivery:

Contributes to the overall direction of the Licensing & Accreditation (L&A) department by applying an equity-focused and Indigenous lens to assess operational priorities, identify candidate and licensee needs, and implement quality assurance measures.
Provides analysis and targeted research on licensing policies, initiatives and changes, to support the effective and equitable application of requirements and to assist staff and candidates in navigating complex or emerging issues in the areas of EDI and access to justice. 
Provides direct, proactive support to licensing candidates, particularly Indigenous candidates and others from equity-deserving groups, by responding to inquiries, identifying and addressing barriers, managing escalations, and supporting candidates through complex or challenging aspects of the licensing process, including requests for accommodation.
Establishes efficient processes and coordinates workflow among employees, consultants, vendors, and practitioners to support timely, consistent and equitable service delivery.
Identifies emerging operational issues related to EDI in licensing and recommends refinements to policies, processes, guidance materials, and initiatives to address them.

Engages internal and external stakeholders by communicating updates and seeking input with respect to licensing and accreditation matters from an EDI perspective.

 
Relationship & Alliance Building:

Serves as a resource on EDI, with a special focus on Indigenous issues, and access to justice for the L&A department and its stakeholders, including candidates, licensees, law schools, colleges, and community groups. 
Develops and maintains collaborative and strategic relationships with key stakeholders and decision-makers, such as external legal organizations and community partners, to articulate the Law Society’s position on EDI in licensing, support consultation and information sharing, and foster goodwill and credibility with the goal of effectively delivering an inclusive licensing and accreditation process.
Leads the planning and implementation of outreach and consultation with Indigenous communities and Indigenous legal service providers as needed.  
Meets regularly with Indigenous communities, the Indigenous bar and other members of the public and the profession to exchange information, develop and implement Indigenous-focused initiatives, and continually expand the network of mutual interest and support.

 
Research:

Stays current on new developments in the field of legal education and licensing, including relevant aspects of practice management and ethics, with particular attention to equity-informed and inclusive approaches and Indigenous issues.  
Monitors emerging educational methodologies, systems, and materials for lectures, seminar groups, computer-assisted learning, and independent study, and contributes to the implementation of innovations for the ongoing improvement of all aspects of the Law Society’s licensing and accreditation activities in ways that enhance accessibility, fairness and inclusion. 

 
Team Membership:

Fosters a collaborative team environment by setting clear goals, encouraging input, recognizing contributions, resolving conflicts, and promoting creativity and problem-solving.
Provides coordination and direction to staff, including program coordinators and others, to ensure the timely and effective delivery of work products.
Shares expertise and presents information to guide and influence the department and internal stakeholders, including licensing staff, working groups, and decision-makers on best practices for EDI in the licensing process.
Supports other special projects and operations as may be required by L&A.

title: Payroll Coordinator, Accounting (12 Month Contract)
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Purpose
The Payroll Coordinator supports the administration of the payroll function.  This includes the processing of the employee, member parental leave assistance program, and bencher payrolls, along with related source deductions and remittances, preparation of pension and benefits remittances, processing of payroll related journal entries, General Ledger account reconciliations, support the T4, T4A, EHT and WSIB reporting processes managed by the Payroll Specialist, and maintenance of payroll and related files and information. In addition to payroll support, the Payroll Coordinator is responsible for the review and processing of bencher expense claims. The position is responsible for the updating of the bencher attendance tracking database used to support reporting to the Audit & Finance Committee. The Payroll Coordinator is also responsible for ongoing correspondence with benchers on expense claim matters as well as communicating with external stakeholders such as the payroll service provider, benefits carriers, auditors, etc. to inquire or resolve issues. The role assists in the preparation of required reporting for benchers and the Audit & Finance Committee, and ad hoc reporting requests for Senior Management and other Committees.
 
Qualifications 
Education and Training   
The minimum level of education required to fulfill the core requirements of this position include a college diploma or university degree in business or accounting. Payroll Compliance Practitioner (PCP) required; Payroll Leadership Professional (PLP) or actively working towards PLP strongly preferred. 
 
Experience
The Payroll Coordinator requires a minimum of 4 years previous related experience in a computerized payroll and benefits administration environment, with solid understanding of general accounting functions. 
 
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

Solid understanding of payroll processes and relevant legislation, benefits administration, source deduction and government remittance procedures
General understanding of general accounting functions, including GAAP / CICA guidelines, accounts payable and financial reporting
Solid understanding of Law Society by-laws and policies as they apply to bencher remuneration, expense reimbursement, payroll and related internal controls
Professional communication skills with the ability to speak and write in a clear, articulate manner when communicating with benchers, adjudicators, and staff
Reason through moderately complex spoken and written information in order to communicate by-law, policy, process and standards of reasonableness information in an audience appropriate format

 
Technical Skills and Knowledge

Thorough knowledge of automated payroll systems and absence management applications, 
Thorough knowledge of personal computers and software applications related to a computerized accounting environment, particularly the use of spreadsheet analyses in support of the finance function and report writing applications
Knowledge of reporting tools such as Crystal reports

  
Key Accountabilities
Client / Customer Service Delivery

Contributes to the development and implementation of integrated payroll processes in support of Law Society client departments and divisions, benchers, and related organizations.  
Works closely with client departments and others to communicate appropriate payroll processes, reviews and verifies payroll information, and contributes to the exchange of information.  
Provides detailed information and reports as required, responds to client inquiries, and follows up to ensure resolution of complaints.  
Remains abreast of Law Society by-laws and policies as well as Canada Revenue Agency statutes, legislation and regulations pertaining to employee payroll, bencher remuneration and expense reimbursement, and communicates the application of same to employees and benchers, (e.g. expense claims allowed, adjusted and disallowed).  
Prepares written communication to benchers and adjudicators related to sensitive expense and remuneration matters.

 
Client / Customer Service Planning

Acts as a subject-matter expert within the Payroll team as well as other departments across the organization on payroll systems, bencher expense reimbursement, and associated guidelines and processes.
Identifies opportunities for improvements within the payroll function, and develops approaches to address these opportunities. 
Monitors and assists in improving and implementing new payroll processes and systems through analysis, research and recommendations. 

 
Financial Responsibility

Processes and validates parental leave, employee and bencher payroll and benefits information, in accordance with Canada Revenue Agency statutes, relevant legislation and regulations, and Law Society policies and procedures.  
Assists the Payroll Specialist in the processing of Law Society payrolls, including the extraction of needed information from the time and attendance application, analyzing and questioning information, following up to gain clarification.  
Processes a full range of transactions and exchanges information with service providers, financial institutions, Law Society client departments, employees, members and benchers to ensure the timely and accurate flow of payrolls (employees, members and benchers).  
Administers retirements, terminations and individual record changes, prepares journal entries, and assists with the reconciliation and issuance of T4 slips.  
Reviews bencher expense claims for authorization and reasonableness, allocates to appropriate expense category and processes for payment.  
Ensures that details of expense claims are accurate and complete, following up with benchers to confirm information, and reconciles approved claims and remuneration payments.  
Processes approved bencher activity sheets for remuneration purposes, calculating appropriate statutory deductions and processing in payroll system.   
Generates canned and develops custom reports using applicable reporting tools in support of informational needs of management and the Audit & Finance Committee, as required, from information residing in the payroll system, time and attendance application or the bencher tracking database.  
For Law Society employee payroll, prepares journals for posting to sub-ledger and general ledgers and uploads the information into the Law Society’s financial system.

 
Team Membership

Actively participates with other members of the department, contributing to department‑wide projects.  
Collaborates with the Payroll Specialist to complete the daily operation of the department, and takes direction from Specialist with respect to Payroll policies, processes and best practices.  
Works cooperatively with client department staff to clarify information and provide assistance regarding payroll procedures, and provide accurate and timely service to benchers, employees, clients and customers. 
Demonstrates flexibility and commitment to the team to maximize resources and support co‑workers during peak periods.

title: Forensic Auditor, Investigation Services
description:
Job Purpose
The Forensic Auditor is an Accounting Specialist engaged in the timely, consistent investigation of a wide range of issues relating to the professional conduct and competence of lawyers and paralegals (“licensees”), in accordance with the Law Society’s public interest mandate, legislation, by-laws and policies.  This includes independent planning, conduct and closure of investigations in a manner consistent with forensic accounting practices, identifying potential breaches by licensees of the Society’s regulations regarding the maintenance of proper accounting records, anti-money laundering, financial schemes, mortgage fraud, syndicated mortgage investment fraud, estates, conflict of interest, and other issues, and providing recommendations regarding further pursuance of files, including settlement and/or discipline of licensees. 
 
QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:

A university degree, or equivalent training and/or experience, coupled with a professional accounting designation, and membership in a recognized Canadian professional accounting body.
As the Forensic Auditor is required to investigate the propriety of complex financial transactions to determine compliance with strict regulatory accounting obligations, the incumbent is required to have a minimum of five years forensic experience, preferably in a regulatory environment.
Required to work out of their home office and on an as-needed basis and attend at licensees’ offices. Incumbents are also required to attend the Law Society’s office as required and directed. There are occasional requirements for overnight travel in the conduct of investigations.

Solid understanding of the Law Society’s mandate, services, legislation and policies.

In-depth understanding of current trends and developments in accounting practices, their practical applications and forensic investigation techniques.

Knowledge of specialized areas such as real estate, estates, mortgage fraud, anti-money laundering and financial schemes.

Knowledge of interview and investigation methodologies, principles, and practices.

Knowledge of a variety of dispute resolution techniques and their appropriate application.

Expressive and persuasive in both spoken and written language in the collection of evidence and facilitation and resolution and disposition of complaints.

Concise, well-organized writing skills in the preparation of a full range of investigative documents and memoranda which may form the basis for disclosure to Litigation Services and agreed statement of fact.

Superior analytical ability.

Able to reason through complex spoken and written information.

Computer literacy, including word processing software, advanced spreadsheet functions, accounting system software and internet search capabilities.
Specific familiarity with Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint and Adobe Pro are definite assets.
Broad understanding of the application of technology preferably in a regulatory/legal environment.

Key Accountabilities
Client / Customer Service Delivery 

Investigates serious and / or complex matters including professional misconduct, conduct unbecoming, competence, licensing, capacity and unauthorized practice. 

Independently plans, conducts and makes recommendations for the disposition of a variety of serious and complex investigative assignments relating to professional conduct and competence, either as a member of an investigation team or as sole investigator. 

Identifies risk and conducts ongoing risk assessments.

Applies the principles of forensic auditing and fraud detection to the investigation and resolution of matters involving allegations of misuse or mishandling of client property entrusted to lawyers. 

Develops case files to prosecutorial and evidentiary standards, including authorization memos, investigation reports, and in the event of prosecution, acts as expert witness at legal and administrative proceedings.  

Assesses the need for and makes recommendations with respect to resolution of investigation files, including but not limited to, establishment of practice controls, seizure of lawyer practices, freezing of lawyer trust accounts, payments made by the Compensation Fund, and license revocation.

Identifies potential candidates for remedial diversion initiatives, seeking out opportunities for alternative dispute resolution and settlement of investigations files. 

Prepares reports for the Proceedings Authorization Committee (PAC) related to non-discipline recommendations (i.e. Invitation to Attend, Regulatory Meeting, Letter of Advice and file closure) and prepares clear and comprehensive Investigative Reports recommending conduct application.

Policy / Regulatory Compliance

Follows procedural and administrative requirements with respect to searches and seizures, including the handling, cataloguing, security, and control of evidence gathered during an investigation. 

Records and produces witness statements in accordance with the Rules and cooperates with Litigation Services’ staff in the preparation of cases for hearing, and testifying as a witness, as required.

Examines and audits accounting records and files maintained by a licensee, identifying issues of compliance with rules, regulations, bylaws and policies.

Performance Goals, Targets and Standards

Contributes to the development of standardized practices, guidelines and procedures in the appropriate conduct and resolution of investigations files from a forensic accounting perspective. 
Conducts own caseload, and works with other members of Investigation Services, as well as colleagues in Intake and Resolution and Litigation Services to establish, monitor and continuously improve processes and case management performance targets. 
Manages a varied and substantial caseload.

Policy Development

Identifies, informs, and advises the Director and Team Managers of Investigation Services of the need for policy development and/or policy change(s) based on analysis of legal issues encountered during investigations. 

As a domain expert, continually assesses policies and procedures, and identifies opportunities for policy development or change in regulation procedures.

Participates in the development of policy and processes when assigned

Team Membership

Works closely with the Team Manager and other Investigation Services staff in the conduct of coordinated investigative and regulatory responses to identified issues involving subjects of investigations.
Promotes the sharing and transfer of knowledge and information amongst team members. 
Acts as an expert witness and advisor in prosecuting forensic audit case files.

Relationship and Alliance Building

Develops and maintains mutually beneficial relationships with law enforcement, government agencies, and various levels of the Federal and Provincial Judicial systems as well as financial institutions to facilitate the exchange of information.

title: Coordinator, Examination Accommodation and Delivery
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Summary:
The Coordinator, Examination Accommodation and Delivery (“Coordinator”), under minimal supervision, is responsible for the delivery of specialized and individualized services to candidates who seek accommodation for the licensing examination based on an enumerated ground listed in the Human Rights Code, R.S.O. 1990. c. H.19 and is accountable for diverse and intricate duties in the administration of the Law Society’s lawyer and paralegal licensing examinations.
The Coordinator follows intricate schedules and protocols, manages sensitive interactions with candidates in high-stake circumstances, and ensures the highest levels of security, accuracy, and confidentiality are met in the management of examination materials and candidate records. The Coordinator is responsible for the review and the approval of examination accommodation requests and the preparation of an accommodation plan.
The Coordinator shares responsibility within the Examination Accommodation team for coordinating examination delivery and participating in the validation of examination documents and results. The Coordinator specializes in an area of examination delivery e.g. paralegal or lawyer licensing examinations that may be situated in Toronto or four other Ontario cities. The Coordinator is responsible for the planning, staffing, and other business operations of delivering examinations, including the selection and contracting of venues and services required for large examination sittings, and providing appropriate training and supervision to large numbers of support personnel.
Qualifications

title: Director, Enterprise Planning and Performance (Permanent)
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Job Purpose 
The Director, Enterprise Planning & Performance will build and manage a small professional team and is charged with strengthening enterprise-wide planning, performance measurement, and transparent reporting on delivery of the Law Society’s Strategic Plan. Reporting to the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director supports the CEO, Executive Committee and Convocation by establishing practical planning rhythms, enterprise-level key performance indicators (KPIs), and disciplined reporting that demonstrates progress against approved strategic objectives in a manner that is clear, transparent and measurable.
The Director works in partnership with operational areas across the organization as well as Business Innovation and Operations Management (BIOM), Information Technology (IT) and Finance as an enterprise integrator, helping to connect priorities, surface interdependencies, and support coordinated execution of the Strategic Plan. Working through influence, the Director helps ensure that planning and reporting processes are coherent, proportionate and supportive of effective delivery.
Key Accountabilities:
1. Enterprise Planning & Performance Framework (Planning)
Under the guidance of the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director provides leadership and expertise to the CEO, Executive Committee, and Convocation to achieve the Law Society’s objectives with respect to enterprise planning, execution discipline, and performance accountability. Establishes and maintains enterprise planning cycles, templates and routines that translate approved strategic priorities into clear initiatives, milestones and measurable outcomes. Supports enterprise prioritization, sequencing and trade-off decisions across initiatives and resources.
2. Enterprise Planning & Accountability Reporting (Delivery)
Coordinates the development, implementation, monitoring and reporting of enterprise-level performance measures and progress against the Strategic Plan, supporting the CEO’s and Executive Committee’s accountability to the Board through clear and measurable reporting. Defines reporting standards to ensure that Strategic Plan accountability is evidence-based, reliable, and consistent over time.
Works in partnership with leaders and teams across the organization as an enterprise integrator to coordinate cross-functional inputs into KPI dashboards, progress updates, and briefing materials that reflect organizational outcomes achieved, delivery risks, mitigation actions, dependencies, and overall confidence in execution of the Strategic Plan. This includes but is not limited to coordination with Policy, Professional Development & Competence, Professional Regulation, Finance, Business Innovation & Operations Management, Information Technology, Communications and others.
3. People Leadership
This senior position supports the Executive Director in ensuring that deliverables will be appropriately operationalized, and that day-to-day mentoring and direction are provided.
Hires, trains, develops and evaluates employees accountable to the Director in accordance with organizational policies and best human resources practices. Fosters a team environment by role modeling leadership behaviour, empowering employees accountable to the Director and building team capability.
4. Financial Responsibility
Assists the Executive Director with developing and monitoring the team’s budget and project-related expenditures, adjusting plans as required to meet fiscal resource constraints.
5. Team Membership
Able to work collaboratively in supporting the CEO, the Executive Committee, and senior leaders, ensuring consistency in enterprise planning and performance reporting across the organization. Works with various internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams, providing leadership and expertise to team members, ensuring broad information and idea exchange.
The Director demonstrates personal excellence, bringing knowledge and functional expertise to the team. Contributes to group decision-making and processes, generating ideas that are strategically sound, integrated with the Law Society’s broader mandate, and achievable in a timely, balanced and fiscally sound manner.
6. Relationship and Alliance Building
Builds credibility and develops effective working relationships with key groups both internally and externally. Partners with operational leaders to support coordination without undermining operational authority. Works closely with Professional Development & Competence and Professional Regulation divisions to understand the core functions of the organization. Where appropriate, supports strategic relationships and shared learning with other regulatory bodies or sector partners on planning, performance measurement and modernization approaches.
Qualifications
Education 
The minimum level of education required to fulfill the core requirements of this position includes a university degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Public Policy, Law or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Experience
The position requires a minimum of 10 years’ progressive related experience gained in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment such as a government, regulatory or complex not-for-profit environment, at least 5 of which are in a managerial / leadership capacity.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

Comprehensive understanding of enterprise planning, performance measurement and reporting in a complex organization, including governance and accountability expectations.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable outcomes, performance indicators, and practical reporting products.
Proven ability to synthesize complex information quickly and communicate it clearly in concise, well-written reports and briefings.
Strong facilitation and relationship management skills; ability to influence without authority and coordinate across functions.
Experience working in highly political situations, managing a variety of viewpoints and sensitivities.
Political astuteness and sound judgment to calibrate intervention—staying light-touch where work is on track and increasing support where delivery is at risk.
Capability to lead, develop and manage a team of professionals, including the conducting of annual team member performance reviews.
Demonstrated ability to assess organizational capability and adjust plans as required to successfully carry out organizational strategies.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple agendas, meet changing deadlines, and deliver on a large number of concurrent commitments.
Superior analytical and communication skills coupled with excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills.

Technical Skills and Knowledge

Computer literacy, including familiarity with email, word processing, spreadsheets, databases and dashboards.
Ability to partner effectively with BIOM/IT on data definitions, reporting automation and CRM-enabled insights.

Collaborates with planners on high level or politically sensitivity planning applications to guide client meetings and to support TRCA’s business objectives

Communicates with team members regularly to assess workload and status of activities, amends work and reassigns staff as needed to direct workflow and accommodate for any situational circumstances.

Education (degree/diploma/certifications/licenses)

University degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field

3+ years progressive managerial experience

The Senior Manager, Operations provides senior leadership and operational command for the Community Safety Unit's 24-hour service-delivery functions. The position ensures that Operations contributes to safe, equitable and healthy TCHC communities through consistent, tenant-centred service delivery.
Reporting to the Senior Director, Community Safety, the Senior Manager, Operations is accountable for the safe and effective delivery of field operations, Dispatch and Investigations, as assigned to the Operations portfolio. The position is responsible for operational command, deployment and service continuity; critical-incident response; workforce leadership; operational performance; and compliance within the portfolio. The Senior Manager translates approved CSU strategies, policies and service standards into operational plans and works with Corporate Services and other functional leads on policy, analytics, training, quality assurance, procurement and program development, while functional accountability for those areas remains with the responsible lead.
 
What you’ll do
 
Operational Command and Service Delivery

Provides senior operational command and oversight for the 24-hour service-delivery functions assigned to Operations, including field operations, Dispatch and Investigations.
Establishes daily operational priorities, deployment plans and resource allocations in accordance with approved CSU strategy, service standards, assessed risk and demand for service.
Maintains service continuity across shifts, manages emerging workload pressures, approves temporary resource reallocations and escalates material capacity or service risks.
Leads the management response to critical incidents, major events and operational emergencies, ensuring timely command, notifications, coordination, documentation and follow-up.
Ensures effective coordination and handoffs among Dispatch, field operations, Investigations and relevant TCHC teams.
Translates approved Community Safety and Well-Being Strategy commitments assigned to Operations into practical service-delivery plans that balance prevention, engagement, de-escalation, diversion and appropriate enforcement.
Coordinates CSU's operational response to fire and life-safety incidents and other corporate emergencies; accountability for the corporate Fire and Life Safety program remains with the designated corporate function.
Participates in the scheduled management on-call rotation and ensures appropriate operational management coverage outside regular working hours.

 
People and Workforce Leadership

Leads and holds accountable the managers and other direct reports assigned to Operations, setting clear expectations for service, conduct, performance and collaboration.
Builds a respectful, equitable, inclusive and psychologically safe working environment that supports employee well-being and effective service to tenants.
Oversees workforce planning, staffing levels, scheduling requirements, attendance management and succession planning for Operations in collaboration with People and Culture and the responsible support functions.
Manages employee performance and conduct within delegated authority, including coaching, performance improvement, recognition and discipline, in accordance with collective agreements and TCHC policies.
Represents Operations in labour-management discussions, grievance processes, recruitment and promotional processes, while working within the authorities of People and Culture, Legal and the Senior Director.
Identifies operational training and competency requirements, ensures staff complete required training and evaluates the application of learning in the workplace without assuming responsibility for administration of the training function.
Ensures appropriate support, debriefing and follow-up for employees affected by critical or traumatic incidents.
Develops the leadership capability of managers and supervisors and promotes consistent management practices across all operational functions and shifts.

 
Operational Performance and Continuous Improvement

Establishes and monitors operational work plans, service standards and performance expectations aligned with approved CSU and TCHC priorities.
Reviews operational information concerning calls for service, dispatch performance, response times, workload, deployment, investigations, report quality and recurring service pressures.
Uses analysis provided by Research and Analytics and other approved data sources to make deployment decisions, identify service gaps and direct corrective action.
Conducts supervisory operational reviews and after-action reviews to identify lessons, improve execution and reduce the recurrence of preventable operational issues.
Implements corrective actions arising from independent quality-assurance reviews, audits, complaints, investigations and other oversight processes applicable to Operations.
Documents operational processes and recommends improvements to procedures, technology, workflows and interdepartmental handoffs.
Provides operational requirements for contracted security services and monitors frontline service performance, escalating contractual, procurement or invoicing matters to the accountable functional owner.
Develops and manages the Operations operating budget, controls expenditures within approved allocations and exercises signing authority in accordance with TCHC policy.
Provides timely operational briefings, critical-incident notifications and performance reports to the Senior Director and other authorized stakeholders.

 
Operational Compliance, Risk and Readiness

Ensures that operational staff comply with the Community Safety and Policing Act, 2019, applicable regulations, Special Constable appointment conditions, the applicable memorandum of understanding, legislation, collective agreements and approved TCHC and CSU policies and procedures.
Identifies, assesses, manages and escalates risks arising from operational activity and implements approved controls within the Operations portfolio.
Ensures that incident reports, investigative records, use-of-force documentation, arrest-related records and other operational records are complete, accurate, timely and handled in accordance with approved requirements.
Ensures that managers and supervisors maintain appropriate oversight of officer conduct, operational decision-making, enforcement activity and adherence to approved authorities.
Assesses operational readiness, including staffing, equipment, technology, communications and contingency requirements, and communicates requirements to the responsible support functions.
Provides operational subject-matter input into the development or revision of policies and procedures and ensures consistent implementation of approved requirements within Operations.
Maintains operational emergency preparedness and business-continuity arrangements for the functions within the portfolio.

 
Operational Partnerships and Coordination

Maintains effective operational relationships with the Toronto Police Service, Toronto Fire Services, paramedic services, emergency-management partners and other public-safety agencies.
Coordinates joint operational activities under approved strategies, agreements and authorities, including incident response, planned deployments and information sharing.
Works with TCHC regional teams, Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation and other internal partners to coordinate operational responses, escalation pathways, follow-up and service handoffs.
Participates in tenant meetings, safety initiatives and community-engagement activities where operational leadership, information or follow-up is required.
Provides operational advice and implementation input to CSU strategy, policy, planning and Community Safety and Well-Being initiatives while respecting the accountability of the responsible functional owner.
Represents Operations on internal and external committees and working groups as assigned.
Performs other operational duties consistent with the purpose and level of the position.

 
What you’ll need
 

Post-secondary degree or diploma in public administration, business administration, criminal justice, criminology, emergency management, sociology or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible operational experience.
A university undergraduate degree and relevant senior-leadership, emergency-management or public-safety credentials are preferred.
Minimum eight years of progressively responsible experience in community safety, public safety, law enforcement, security, emergency management or a similarly complex service environment, including at least five years leading managers or supervisors in a unionized, 24-hour operation.
Demonstrated experience directing multi-function operations, workforce deployment, service continuity and shift-based response in a complex organization.
Demonstrated experience managing critical incidents, operational emergencies and time-sensitive decisions involving public and employee safety.
Strong people-leadership capability, including performance management, coaching, succession planning, attendance management, employee relations and discipline.
Working knowledge of collective agreements and experience participating in labour-management, grievance, recruitment and promotional processes.
Comprehensive knowledge of community-safety and law-enforcement operations, including incident response, investigations, enforcement authorities, de-escalation and operational risk management.
Knowledge of the legislative and governance framework applicable to Special Constables, including appointment conditions, oversight requirements and the applicable memorandum of understanding.
Demonstrated ability to balance prevention, engagement, de-escalation, diversion and appropriate enforcement when serving diverse communities.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret operational data, assess service performance and direct evidence-informed improvements.
Demonstrated experience managing operational budgets and allocating staffing, equipment and other resources within delegated authority.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to prepare executive briefings and communicate effectively with tenants, employees, senior leaders, elected officials, unions and external agencies.
Strong negotiation, facilitation, conflict-resolution, mediation and relationship-building skills.
Ability to exercise sound judgement, discretion, tact and composure while working under pressure in a complex and highly visible environment.
Possession of a valid, non-probationary Province of Ontario Class G driver's licence in good standing and ability to satisfy all screening and eligibility requirements associated with the position and Special Constable appointment.

To apply you do not need experience in all three areas.
About the Supervision Department
The payments landscape in Canada and globally is evolving rapidly, driven by technological advancements that are introducing innovative ways for consumers and businesses to make payments. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), the Bank of Canada is responsible for registering retail payment service providers (PSPs) that perform retail payment activities, maintaining a public registry of PSPs, and supervising PSPs’ compliance with operational risk management, fund safeguarding and reporting requirements.
The Bank assesses whether PSPs are managing risks effectively, identifies areas for improvement, and promotes compliance through a range of supervisory, compliance and enforcement tools. These positions will support the ongoing implementation and continuous improvement of the Retail Payments Supervisory Framework.
What you will do
As a Supervisor within Retail Payments Supervision, you will contribute to fulfilling the Bank’s regulatory mandate by supporting work across one or more areas of Registration, Risk Supervision and Enforcement. You will apply supervisory judgment, strong analysis and sound recommendations to help implement the Bank’s legislative and regulatory authorities under the RPAA.
Depending on the area of focus, you may assess registration applications and scope questions, evaluate PSPs’ operational risk and fund safeguarding practices, review PSP reporting and incidents, investigate potential non-compliance, or support the use of appropriate supervisory, compliance and enforcement tools. You will also contribute to policies, procedures, guidance, training materials and process improvements that strengthen the Bank’s approach to supervising PSPs.
Apply technical expertise and knowledge of supervisory concepts, principles, practices and methodologies aligned to the Bank’s Supervisory Framework.
Analyze complex information, identify issues and trends, and develop recommendations for Senior Supervisors, Principal Supervisors, Directors and Executives.
Collaborate with colleagues and internal or external partners to support registration, supervision, compliance and enforcement activities.
Contribute to business documentation, operational policies, procedures, guidance, training materials and continuous improvement initiatives.
What you need
As an innovative and self-motivated problem solver, you can understand, interpret and analyze complex information and issues, exercise sound judgment, and provide clear recommendations. You communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with a broad range of audiences. You are equally comfortable working collaboratively within a team or independently, and you bring strong attention to detail while working under tight timelines.
You have the desire to build the knowledge of the broader financial system, the retail payments ecosystem, retail payment service providers, and the role of regulation and supervision in maintaining a well-functioning system. You are flexible, adaptable and able to align your actions with the needs, priorities and goals of a new and evolving mandate.
What you need to succeed
Experience interpreting and applying legislation, regulations, guidance, policies or supervisory frameworks.
Experience conducting analysis, identifying discrepancies or trends, synthesizing information, and recommending practical solutions.
Experience in one or more of registration, risk management, compliance, enforcement, audit, assurance, controls review, or financial sector supervision.
Ability to work within ambiguity, manage changing priorities and produce high-quality analysis and documentation.
Nice to have
Knowledge of, or experience with, supervisory frameworks that include registration, risk supervision, compliance or enforcement regimes.
Experience with administrative law regimes or working with or for a regulator, PSP, financial institution, fintech or paytech.
Experience in operational or cyber risk management, fund safeguarding, client asset protection, trust or custodial account oversight, audit, assurance, controls review, compliance or enforcement.
E
xperience working with data sets, reporting, data visualization or business documentation.
A background or designation in law, finance, accounting, economics, business administration, risk, audit, compliance  or enforcement.
Interest in supervisory technology, including artificial intelligence to support efficient supervisory practices

The position requires a minimum of four years of relevant work experience, as well as a bachelor’s degree in law, finance, accounting, economics, business administration or another relevant field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.

description:
Analyst, Retail Payments Supervision
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers:
Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our
Recruitment process
.
In addition to the position being staffed, this competition may be used to fill similar opportunities (Regular or Term) that become available at the same job grade. If you’re interested in this type of role, we encourage you to apply.
About the Supervision Department
The payments landscape in Canada and globally is evolving rapidly, driven by technological advancements that are introducing innovative ways for consumers and businesses to make payments. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), the Bank of Canada is responsible for registering retail payment service providers (PSPs) that perform retail payment activities, maintaining a public registry of PSPs, and ensuring PSPs’ compliance with operational risk management, fund safeguarding and reporting requirements.
The Bank assesses whether PSPs are managing risks effectively, identifies areas for improvement, and promotes compliance through a range of supervisory, compliance and enforcement tools. These positions will support the ongoing implementation and continuous improvement of the Retail Payments Supervisory Framework.
What you will do
As an Analyst within Retail Payments Supervision, you will contribute to fulfilling the Bank’s regulatory mandate by supporting work across one or more areas of Registration, Risk Supervision and Enforcement. You will conduct analysis and support the development of sound recommendations to help fulfil the Bank’s legislative and regulatory authorities under the RPAA.
Depending on the area of focus, you may assess registration applications and scope questions, support the evaluation of PSPs’ operational risk management and fund safeguarding practices, review PSP reporting and incidents, investigate potential non-compliance, or support the use of appropriate supervisory and enforcement tools. As an analyst, you will:
Analyze issues relating to the Bank’s supervision of PSPs
Contribute to business documentation, operational policies, procedures, guidance, training materials, and continuous improvement initiatives
Collaborate with colleagues and internal or external partners to support registration, supervision, compliance and enforcement activities
Contribute to the development of recommendations to support decision making
What you need to succeed
You have a desire to build your knowledge of the broader financial system, the retail payments ecosystem, financial technology, PSPs, and the role of regulation and supervision in maintaining a well-functioning system. You are flexible, adaptable, and able to align your actions with the needs, priorities, and goals of the Bank’s supervisory mandate.
As an innovative and self-motivated problem solver, you can synthesize and interpret complex information and issues. You bring strong attention to detail while working under tight timelines. You can organize and balance a variety of tasks and are equally comfortable working collaboratively within a team or independently. You communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with a broad range of audiences.
Nice-to-have
Experience working with data sets, reporting, data visualization, or business documentation
Knowledge of retail payments, financial technology firms, or payment clearing and settlement systems (financial market infrastructures)
A background or designation in law, finance, accounting, economics, business administration, risk, audit, compliance, or enforcement
Interest in supervisory technology, including artificial intelligence, to support efficient supervisory practices
Your education and experience
The position requires a bachelor’s degree in law, finance, accounting, economics, business administration, or an equivalent degree in a relevant field, with a minimum of two years’ experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement
T
he
Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French.  The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional).  If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level.  Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents
Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Reliability
Relocation assistance may be provided, if required
Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us
This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit
A great deal to consider
.
Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $73,511 to $86,484 (job grade 14)
The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at  5 to 7% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (3%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay.
Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health, dental disability and life and/or accident insurance coverage that meets your needs
Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement
Indexed, defined-benefit pension
