title: Lead, OVIN Incubators
description:
Who We Are:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) was established in 1987 and is a leading not-for-profit organization that works with industry, academia, and government. OCI focuses on ensuring that the people of Ontario reap the personal and economic benefits of leading-edge research underway at our publicly funded universities, colleges, and research hospitals - research that can be transformed into technologies and services that enhance quality of life and help build a globally competitive, job-creating economy in Ontario.
Specifically, OCI supports the commercialization of academic intellectual property (IP), industry-academic collaborations, and the development and adoption of emerging technologies. This includes overseeing the execution of advanced technology platforms that will equip Ontario companies to compete in a competitive global digital economy.
We also support and invest in early-stage projects where the probability of commercial success and investment return on innovation are substantial. OCI’s strong expertise in de-risking innovation helps attract private investors and other funders to new ventures, bolstering their success. We also contribute to the development and retention of talent to ensure that industry has access to personnel with the most advanced skills and knowledge and that highly trained personnel find opportunities to apply their expertise in Ontario.
OCI leads the Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network (OVIN) initiative on behalf of the Government of Ontario. OVIN builds upon Ontario’s position as a world-leading automotive manufacturing and supply jurisdiction in addition to the large cluster of information and communication technology companies operating in the province. Ontario’s high-quality post-secondary institutions, first class talent, innovative small and medium sized enterprises, and infrastructure to support entrepreneurship ensure that the province is uniquely positioned to capture the economic opportunity of the automotive technology and smart mobility innovation space and lead the global mobility transformation.
Through resources such as research and development (R&D) funding, talent development, technology acceleration, business and technical supports, and demonstration grounds, OVIN provides a competitive advantage to Ontario-based automotive and mobility companies – allowing Ontario to reinforce its position as a North American leader in transformative automotive technologies, as well as transportation and infrastructure systems.
The Opportunity:
OVIN, in collaboration with industry partners, post-secondary institutions, municipalities and regional stakeholders is launching automotive and mobility incubators, designed to:
Foster a collaborative ecosystem where researchers, entrepreneurs, startups and scale-ups can systematically engage with industry
Support research and the commercialization of IP through interdisciplinary projects
Support the translation of IP and new technologies into the creation of new ventures across the province
Provide resources and programming to support the success and viability of new ventures and regional incubation and acceleration space in the province
Reporting to the Manager, Incubators, the Lead, OVIN Incubators will be the regional representative for all incubator activities, manage the day-to-operations, and play a coordinating role between all key stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
The Lead is expected to assume operational responsibilities, including, but not limited to:
Support the Manager on the strategic planning and design of OVIN Incubators, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives.
Apply knowledge of research commercialization and start-up incubation/acceleration to make recommendations on program development, execution and improvements, in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
Develop and maintain a database of enterprises active in the sector.
Develop and maintain a database of academic researchers active in the sector.
Pursue extensive outreach to enterprises in the sector.
Develop and manage the incubator intake and review processes, timelines, program budgets and the day-to-day delivery of the program.
Work collaboratively and liaise with incubator partners, including members of industry and post-secondary institutions, to ensure that key requirements are defined, and program delivery executed within the appropriate framework.
Execute on the promotion of incubator programming, working in tandem with the key stakeholders and departments within OCI.
Support steering committee and other stakeholder meetings.
Support OCI/ OVIN Incubator presence at external events and functions, including delivering content at meetings, workshops, and events in support of incubator programming.
Work cross-functionally across departments and collaboratively with other OCI staff (Business Development Operations, Programs, and MARCOM etc.).
Manage program stewardship, including program monitoring and metrics, outcomes, and impacts for internal strategy and external reporting.
Support Manager to identify and manage program outcomes, and work with marketing and communications teams to develop success stories.
May be required to perform other related duties as assigned.
Qualifications
:
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Business, Technology, Project Management).
3-5 years experience in program management, incubators, start-up/SME support or technology/IP development particularly in: automotive and mobility, research projects or technology integration.
Strong project management skills, including budgeting, scheduling, and resource allocation.
Excellent communication and presentation abilities.
Problem-solving abilities and adaptability in a dynamic environment.
Highly developed, interpretive and analytical skills in MS Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
Innovation, technology commercialization, or entrepreneurship program management experience; experience with automotive and mobility programs would be a strong asset.
Occasional requirement to attend events outside of normal business hours.
Occasional travel within Ontario.
Competencies:
Team player with highly developed interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively and collaborate with people at all levels within the organization and externally.
Demonstrated high degree of initiative, efficient, organized and able to produce high quality work under pressure in a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage numerous conflicting and changing priorities simultaneously.
Ability to work with minimal supervision and take accountability to address obstacles and overcome barriers by identifying possible resolution options and alternatives.
Intellectually curious about developments and trends in a sector.
Able to demonstrate integrity and ethics in decision making and in relationships with colleagues and clients.
Able to reflect and promote OCI’s values through work with colleagues, clients and stakeholders.
Embody OCI’s commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI).

title: Manager, Innovation Strategy & Insights
description:
Who
We
Are:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI), established in 1987, is a leading not-for-profit organization that works with industry, academia, and government. OCI focuses on ensuring that the people of Ontario reap the personal and economic benefits of leading-edge research underway at our publicly funded universities, colleges, and research hospitals - research that can be transformed into technologies and services that enhance quality of life and help build a globally competitive, job-creating economy in Ontario.
Specifically, OCI supports the commercialization of academic intellectual property (IP), industry-academic collaborations, and the development and adoption of emerging technologies. This includes overseeing the execution of advanced technology platforms that will equip Ontario companies to compete in a competitive global digital economy.
We also support and invest in early-stage projects where the probability of commercial success and investment return on innovation are substantial. OCI’s strong expertise in de-risking innovation helps attract private investors and other funders to new ventures, bolstering their success. We contribute as well to the development and retention of talent to ensure that industry has access to personnel with the most advanced skills and knowledge and that highly trained personnel find opportunities to apply their expertise in Ontario.
OCI leads Ontario’s Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network (OVIN) initiative on behalf of the Government of Ontario. OVIN builds upon Ontario’s position as a world-leading automotive manufacturing and supply jurisdiction in addition to the large cluster of information and communication technology companies operating in the province. Ontario’s high-quality post-secondary institutions, first class talent, innovative small and medium sized enterprises, and infrastructure to support entrepreneurship ensure that the province is uniquely positioned to capture the economic opportunity of the automotive technology and smart mobility innovation space and lead the global mobility transformation.
Through resources such as research and development (R&D) funding, talent development, technology acceleration, business and technical supports, and demonstration grounds, OVIN provides a competitive advantage to Ontario-based automotive and mobility companies – allowing Ontario to reinforce its position as a North American leader in transformative automotive technologies, as well as transportation and infrastructure systems.

description:

Manager, Strategic Sponsorship
s
leads the development and execution of sponsorship and funding strategies for DiscoveryX, Ontario’s premier innovation showcase and conference, and other Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) marketing and communications initiatives.

Working across Marketing & Communications, Business Development, Programs, Strategic Initiatives, and Executive Leadership, the Manager will help position OCI as Ontario's premier innovation convenor while developing sustainable, year-round sponsorship revenue streams.
Who We Are
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is the province’s leading innovation engine, bringing together industry, academia, government, and investors to accelerate commercialization and scale Ontario-made technologies.
From AI and quantum to life sciences, cleantech, and advanced manufacturing, OCI powers the programs and partnerships helping Ontario companies grow, compete globally, and build the future, right here.

title: Program Portfolio Manager, Auto & Mobility- 9 month contract
description:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) drives the development of Ontario’s economy by helping create new jobs, products, services, technologies, and businesses. In partnership with industry, OCI co-invests to commercialize innovation originating in the province’s publicly funded colleges, universities, and research hospitals. We also support and invest in early-stage projects, where the probability of commercial success and potential total return on innovation are substantial. Another expanding focus for OCI is the development of the next generation of innovators through our entrepreneurship fellowships and programs for students and youth across Ontario. OCI’s efforts are focused on sectors of the economy with the greatest potential to drive Ontario’s future prosperity and global competitiveness: energy and environment (including water); advanced manufacturing; advanced health technologies; and information, communications technologies, and digital media. A trusted partner of government in program delivery, we are committed to advancing a whole-of-government approach as a means of streamlining funding application processes for companies and entrepreneurs.
OVIN (Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network), led by OCI, is the Government of Ontario’s flagship initiative to support the future of the automotive and mobility sector. Through innovative programming, business and technical supports, and testing and demonstration sites, the OVIN initiative is driving the commercialization of advanced technologies, cultivating the capacity of a province-wide network to drive future mobility solutions and addressing the evolving needs of Ontario's automotive and mobility sector's workforce.
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Director, Strategy & Programs - Automotive and Mobility, the Program Portfolio Manager in this contract role is responsible for the day-to-day execution of programs within the Automotive and Mobility portfolio, with additional outward-facing program oversight responsibilities with funders and projects, including project monitoring, program administration activities, and stakeholder relations. This role will work within existing financial and program administration processes and frameworks to ensure organizational efficiencies are maintained and/or maximized and that there is full alignment across all programs and initiatives.
Key Job Responsibilities:
Lead the delivery, review, and continuous improvement of OVIN’s communications strategy, including the development of communication assets, such as press releases, briefing documents, social media posts, speaker notes and keynote presentations.
Engage stakeholders in the creation and execution of industry-leading events and education opportunities (conferences, meetups, workshops, panels, hackathons, best practices, etc.).
Working in with the OCI Marcom team, manage the development of creative assets, marketing collateral, promotional videos, and other relevant products.
Working with Strategic Programs and Workforce Planning and Talent Strategy teams, support the planning, design, development, and deployment of promotion of programs, partnership opportunities and strategic initiatives.
Engage, develop, and maintain strong networks with stakeholders in the automotive and mobility sector, including individual and corporate contacts, post-secondary institutions, research partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
Foster and identify partnership opportunities with industry to benefit OCI and the ventures we support including automotive and mobility industry organizations and government bodies.
Identify conferences, speaking, media, and publication opportunities to promote and address the needs of our stakeholders and promote the OVIN/OCI brand.
Keep abreast of industry and/or domain knowledge and activities, including current events, breakthroughs, trends, regulatory issues and key contacts and possess a solid understanding of the global industry to support thought leadership.
Provide regular updates to senior leadership, communicating opportunities and escalating risks when appropriate.
Interface and liaise with stakeholders; work cross-functionally across departments to assemble resources and ensure the successful delivery of projects
Identify, develop and manage outcomes, and work with the OCI Marcom team to develop, communicate and publish success stories.
Other related duties as assigned, with occasional requirements to attend events outside of normal business hours, and occasional travel within Ontario.
Skills and Competencies:
Formal, specialized education (4-year university degree).
Minimum of 5 years of related experience in the management or execution of programs and initiatives.
Innovation, technology commercialization, or entrepreneurship program management experience; experience with automotive and mobility programs would be a strong asset.
Client and stakeholder relationship management experience particularly working with senior level private and public sector representatives.
Process oriented, with superior operational experience.
Superior project oversight and time management skills, including executing and monitoring program activities in order to accomplish program objectives within constraints such as time, budget, and quality standards.
Strong oral and written communication skills.

Consummate professional, able to represent the organization in all circumstances.
Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with internal and external teams.

TVO Media Education Group (

Who we are
We are an agency of the Ontario Ministry of Education and a registered charity that contributes to learning, civic engagement, and public service media across Ontario. We provide free, trusted, and accessible educational content that can support Ontarians of all ages, regardless of background, location, or circumstance. To fulfill our mandate, TVO delivers curriculum-connected resources through TVO Learn and TVOkids, offers Ontario’s largest online high school through TVO ILC, and produces journalism, documentaries, current affairs programming, and podcasts with TVO Today that help Ontarians understand the issues shaping their communities.
What we’re looking for
Are you a high-energy relationship builder with the ability to inspire donors? Do you enjoy creating meaningful connections and engaging donors with an organization’s mission? TVO is seeking a passionate, collaborative, and results-oriented fundraising professional to manage our monthly and midlevel donor portfolios. Does this describe you? If so, we want to hear from you.
The Development Officer, Monthly and Midlevel Giving will be responsible for growing revenue and strengthening TVO’s community of loyal supporters. The incumbent will manage a portfolio of monthly and midlevel donors and prospects, engaging them with TVO’s programs and impact to encourage renewed and increased support. Using a mix of personalized outreach, direct marketing, and digital engagement, the Development Officer will provide thoughtful stewardship and create meaningful opportunities for donors to connect with TVO’s mission.
How you will make an impact
Manage a portfolio of 500+ monthly and midlevel donors and prospects, with responsibility for achieving annual revenue, retention, renewal, and upgrade goals
Develop and implement annual strategies and workplans for monthly and midlevel donor engagement in collaboration with the Manager, Annual Giving
Engage donors with TVO’s programs and impact to deepen their connection to the organization and inspire continued support
Encourage donors to renew and increase their support through thoughtful, timely, and relevant communications
Develop and implement strategies to grow TVO’s monthly giving program, including donor acquisition, conversion, upgrading, reactivation, retention, and recognition
Review annual giving campaign responses and donor data to identify and qualify new monthly and Midlevel prospects
Identify monthly and midlevel donors with the interest and capacity to become major or legacy giving prospects
Plan and support donor stewardship activities and events

Collaborate with Marketing, Communications, and other internal teams to develop donor communications, engagement opportunities, and stewardship materials
Oversee and contribute to the creative development, messaging, and segmentation of monthly and midlevel donor mailings, emails and outreach campaigns
Monitor and report on program performance, donor activity, and campaign results, recommending opportunities to strengthen engagement and increase revenue
Maintain accurate and timely donor records, contact reports, and portfolio activity in Raiser’s Edge and related systems
Conduct ongoing evaluation of TVO’s monthly and midlevel giving programs and recommend improvements to program design, donor journeys, and engagement strategies
Ensure fundraising activities reflect donor stewardship standards, ethical fundraising practices, and TVO’s corporate and legal requirements
Ensure vendor and supplier agreements meet TVO’s corporate and legal requirements
What you will bring to TVO
Minimum of three years of fundraising, donor relations, or donor stewardship experience
Knowledge of fundamental fundraising practices, including donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship
Demonstrated ability to build strong relationships and engage donors
A genuine interest in learning about donors’ motivations, interests, and connection to TVO’s mission
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to initiate conversations and make personalized fundraising asks
Experience managing a donor portfolio and developing tailored engagement or stewardship strategies
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously

Resourceful, proactive, and comfortable working independently with minimal supervision
Collaborative and able to work effectively with colleagues across teams and departments
Flexible and solutions-oriented, with the ability to anticipate, identify, and resolve problems
Demonstrates TVO’s values of Excellence & Innovation, Ownership, Collaboration, Trust and Respect
What we offer
Working at TVO, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work that impacts millions of Ontarians. You’ll belong to a diverse, tight-knit community of talented colleagues who share a passion for education. With learning at the centre of everything we do, we invest in developing our people and promoting a culture of continuous learning. You might even get to meet Polkaroo!
We hope you’ll consider joining us.
Applications will be accepted until 4:00pm on September 30, 2026.
Not sure you have everything we’re asking for, but know you can make a big impact? We encourage you to apply for consideration.

TVO is an agency of the Ontario Ministry of Education. Reporting to the Director, Corporate Communications, the Manager, External Communications is responsible for building and managing TVO’s public relations strategies, a critical role in the organization’s communications team. Support TVO executives and divisional leaders with external speaking opportunities and media message preparation.
Support issues management by monitoring external conversations, developing clear messaging and response strategies to help mitigate reputational risk.
Oversee preparation of media monitoring reports for campaigns, monthly and quarterly reporting.
Coach and mentor junior team members and support their overall professional growth.
What you will bring to TVO
University degree (or equivalent) preferably in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism or related field.

title: AV Technician & Media Production Assistant
description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum, ranking among the top 10 cultural institutions in North America. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement. As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost 21st-century museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking an AV Technician & Media Production Assistant to support audiovisual operations and media production initiatives across the museum.
Reporting to the Manager, Media Productions, this role is responsible for maintaining and supporting audiovisual systems across exhibitions, galleries, public venues, and events, while also assisting with media production workflows and digital asset management.
The successful candidate will help ensure audiovisual experiences operate reliably and effectively while supporting the creation, organization, and delivery of media content for exhibitions, programming, and institutional initiatives.
This is an ideal opportunity for an early-career audiovisual or media production professional looking to work at the intersection of technology, storytelling, and visitor experience.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Monitor, maintain, troubleshoot, and support audiovisual systems throughout exhibitions, galleries, and public spaces
Assist with the installation, configuration, testing, and decommissioning of audiovisual equipment, including projectors, displays, audio systems, media players, and interactive technologies
Provide technical support for museum events, programs, meetings, performances, and venue rentals
Conduct routine system checks, identify technical issues, and coordinate repairs or maintenance to minimize downtime
Maintain accurate inventories, usage logs, and documentation for audiovisual equipment and systems
Support media production projects through equipment preparation, on-location capture assistance, lighting and audio support, and data management
Collaborate with internal teams, contractors, vendors, and presenters to ensure successful delivery of exhibitions, installations, and events
Contribute to the continuous improvement of AV operations, media workflows, and documentation practices
WHAT YOU BRING
Completion of a two-year college diploma in multimedia production, audio engineering, audiovisual technology, technical theatre, broadcasting, media production, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
2–3 years of experience supporting audiovisual systems, media production, live events, or technical production environments
Working knowledge of audiovisual hardware, including projectors, displays, touchscreens, audio systems, media players, videowalls, and related technologies
Experience troubleshooting AV systems and supporting show control, playback, or control software
Foundational knowledge of video, audio, and media production workflows, including equipment setup, file management, ingest, and delivery
Experience supporting video and audio capture in studio, gallery, event, or production environments
Familiarity with media asset management, file organization, digital archives, and naming conventions
Strong computer skills, including experience with PC and Mac operating systems and Microsoft Office applications
Strong organizational, communication, and customer service skills
Ability to prioritize multiple requests and work effectively in fast-paced environments
Ability to work independently while collaborating with cross-functional teams
Ability to regularly work evenings and weekends to support exhibitions, installations, and events
Ability to lift and move equipment, work at heights when required, and remain standing for extended periods during installations and event support
WHAT WE OFFER
Comprehensive benefits coverage:
For permanent and full-time contract positions (conditions apply), enjoy paid benefits for individuals and families, a health spending account, and an Employee Assistance Program.
Perks:
Free ROM membership for permanent full-time and part-time staff, plus discounts to over 200 attractions through Attractions Ontario.
And more!
SALARY & TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT
START DATE: October 2026
OPEN DATE: August 26, 2026
CLOSE DATE: September 11, 2026
STATUS: Part-time, permanent
EMPLOYEE GROUP: OPSEU
EXPECTED COMPENSATION: $28.09 - $32.09 hourly
SCHEDULE: Up to 24 hours weekly
PROBATIONARY PERIOD: 420 hours or six (6) months
LOCATION (onsite): Toronto, ON
WHAT TO EXPECT IN OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS
Initial conversation:
A 30-minute virtual conversation** with a Recruiter to discuss your interest in the role and ROM and how you can make an impact.
Second interview:
A 1-hour in-person meeting with the Hiring Manager and relevant team members. You may be asked to present a pre-assigned case study and discuss scenarios relevant to your role. Depending on the position, you might also be given a tour of ROM and receive a preview of your responsibilities and interactions.
Third Interview
(if required): a final interview with key stakeholders.
The above-listed process may change or vary based on the nature and scope of the position.
**All virtual conversations and interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams and may be recorded.**
WHY PEOPLE CHOOSE ROM
Cultural engagement:
Daily interactions with Toronto's diverse culture and international visitors offer insights into social and cultural trends. We champion inclusive community programs and connections through diverse experiences.
Continuous learning:
At ROM, expertise and continuous skill development are paramount. Our culture of curiosity and open-mindedness fosters growth beyond traditional career paths.
Passion & fulfillment:
Our work in preserving and curating cultural narratives brings deep satisfaction. We are passionate about the arts, global history, cultural diversity, and leveraging digital technologies to enhance accessibility.

WHO WE ARE
Royal Ontario Museum
(ROM) is Canada’s premier museum, featuring a comprehensive collection of Art, Culture and Nature. Among the top 10 cultural institutions in North America, ROM has a world-class collection of 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, featured in 40 gallery and exhibition spaces. ROM's mission is to transform lives by helping people to understand the past, make sense of the present, and come together to shape a shared future. The museum is known globally for expanding the boundaries of knowledge and presenting it in new and innovative ways across the intersecting worlds of art, culture, and nature.

Evolving for the 21st Century
ROM’s vision is to become a distinctly twenty-first century museum, one that is globally recognized for expanding the boundaries of knowledge, fostering innovation in presenting that knowledge, and increasing public relevance within the intersecting worlds of art, culture, and nature.
To realize this vision, ROM has adopted a strategic direction that builds on its strengths and capabilities while evolving in step with a rapidly changing world. The Museum is becoming an ever more outward-facing institution, focused on playing a central role in community and cultural life, while increasing artistic, cultural, and scientific impact both nationally and internationally. ROM's extensive exhibition schedule and public programs attract approximately 190,000 students and a total average attendance of more than one million visitors annually. As the country’s preeminent field research institution and an international leader in collections-based discoveries, ROM builds and shares global collections, creates knowledge, inspires learning, encourages gathering, and sparks exchange on topics that matter to people and communities.
Situated in the most diverse major city in the world, Toronto, within a province and country known for pluralism, openness, and global perspectives, ROM is well positioned for the future and for an even larger role on the world stage, encouraging greater engagement through inclusion and transdisciplinary thinking. Learn more about

.
Curator of Insects & Arachnids
10M specimens
WHO WE NEED
Royal Ontario Museum is seeking an innovative and collaborative Curator of Insects & Arachnids to lead one of North America's most significant entomological collections and advance research, public engagement, and collections stewardship in this globally important field.
Home to more than 10 million insect and arachnid specimens, ROM's collection is internationally recognized for its breadth, scientific value, and contribution to research in taxonomy, systematics, ecology, evolution, conservation, and biodiversity. As Curator, you will build upon this extraordinary resource through original research, strategic collection development, exhibitions, public programming, and partnerships that connect people to the natural world.
This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished scientist with a passion for collections-based research and science communication to shape the future of one of Canada's premier natural history collections. Working within ROM's highly collaborative Department of Natural History, you will partner across disciplines, including art, culture, and nature, to develop exhibitions, inspire learning, mentor emerging researchers, and engage diverse audiences, all while contributing to internationally recognized scholarship.
The successful candidate will bring an established or emerging research program, a collaborative mindset, and a strong commitment to sharing knowledge through research, exhibitions, education, and community engagement. Opportunities may also exist for a university cross-appointment and eligibility to pursue external research funding, including through the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC).
Exceptional early-career and mid-career scientists are encouraged to apply.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Lead the stewardship, strategic growth, and long-term vision of ROM's internationally significant Insects & Arachnids collection, ensuring its continued excellence in research, preservation, accessibility, and public value.
Conduct and publish original, collections-based research in arthropod taxonomy, systematics, ecology, evolution, conservation biology, and related disciplines while securing external research funding.
Develop innovative exhibitions, public programs, and educational initiatives that connect diverse audiences to the importance of insects and arachnids and their role in biodiversity, sustainability, and human society.
Collaborate across ROM's curatorial, collections, exhibitions, education, and programming teams to create interdisciplinary experiences that bridge art, culture, and nature.
Build meaningful partnerships with universities, Indigenous communities, researchers, government agencies, and other organizations to advance research, knowledge sharing, and community engagement.
Champion public scholarship by serving as an engaging spokesperson for ROM through presentations, media, publications, and outreach initiatives.
Mentor and supervise students, interns, volunteers, and staff while fostering the next generation of scientists and museum professionals.
Contribute to fundraising, grant development, and strategic initiatives that support the continued growth and impact of ROM's Natural History programs.
Maintain active involvement in national and international scientific, scholarly, and museum communities to strengthen ROM's global reputation.
WHAT YOU BRING
PhD (or equivalent) in arthropod systematics, ecology, conservation biology, or a closely related field, with expertise in arthropod taxonomy and phylogenetics.
Demonstrated research excellence with a record of scholarly publications and the potential to establish or expand an externally funded research program.
At least one year of postdoctoral or equivalent professional experience within a museum, university, government, NGO, or similarly research-intensive environment.
Experience working with natural history collections and applying collections-based research to advance scientific knowledge and public understanding.
Strong interest or experience in developing museum exhibitions, public programming, and science communication for diverse audiences.
Excellent collaboration, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across disciplines and with internal and external partners.
Experience mentoring or supervising students, interns, volunteers, or research staff.
Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, and collaborative engagement, including an interest in working with Indigenous communities and diverse partners.
Preferred Assets
Expertise in molecular and genomic methods, including DNA analysis, phylogenomics, comparative genomics, or historical biogeography.
Experience securing competitive research grants or philanthropic funding.
Knowledge of museum collections management, digitization initiatives, and museum ethics.
Experience integrating conservation, sustainability, or biodiversity research into public engagement initiatives.
Eligibility for a university cross-appointment and/or NSERC funding.
International research collaborations and cross-cultural experience.

title: Senior Conservator (18-month Contract)
description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement. As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking a Senior Conservator of Organic Objects to provide advanced conservation expertise and leadership in the preservation, examination, treatment, and preventive care of objects in ROM’s collections and temporary custody.
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Conservation, you will independently assess complex conservation needs, develop and execute treatments, establish preservation standards, conduct and interpret technical research, and provide expert guidance across the Museum. You will play an integral role in exhibitions, galleries, acquisitions, loans, collections care, emergency response, and major institutional projects while balancing preservation requirements with access, interpretation, and operational needs.
As a senior member of the Conservation team, you will also oversee the effective operation of a conservation laboratory, establish priorities and workflows, and provide guidance and supervision to conservators, interns, volunteers, and project staff as required. This is an opportunity for an accomplished conservation professional to contribute deep technical expertise, sound judgment, and leadership to the stewardship of internationally significant collections.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Examine collection objects, assess their condition and conservation needs, and develop and perform appropriate treatments supported by thorough written and photographic documentation
Establish and apply preventive conservation standards for environmental conditions, handling, storage, mounting, display, packing, transportation, exhibitions, and loans
Conduct technical examination and conservation research into object materials, manufacture, deterioration, treatment methods, and conservation materials, including coordinating and interpreting scientific analysis
Provide conservation expertise for exhibitions, galleries, acquisitions, loans, collections moves, storage improvements, and other major museum initiatives
Collaborate with curators, designers, collections professionals, and project teams to balance preservation requirements with access, interpretation, and operational needs
Survey collections, assess risks, establish conservation priorities, and contribute to preventive conservation, emergency preparedness and emergency response
Lead the effective operation of the conservation laboratory, managing workflows, priorities, equipment, supplies, budgets, and resource requirements
Supervise, mentor, and provide technical guidance to junior conservators, interns, volunteers, and project staff as required
Advance conservation knowledge and practice through research, professional development, publications, presentations, consultations, and public or educational programming
WHAT YOU BRING
Master's Degree in Conservation with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience, specializing in the conservation of organic objects; at least 3 years in a museum setting preferred. Alternatively, a combination of education and experience deemed acceptable.
Advanced expertise in Organic Object conservation specialization, including object materials and fabrication techniques, deterioration processes, examination, preservation, and treatment
Excellent knowledge of conservation treatment theory and practice, preventive conservation, and professional standards and ethics, including the CAC/CAPC Code of Ethics and Guidance for Practice
Demonstrated ability to assess complex conservation problems, exercise sound professional judgment, and independently plan and execute treatments
Experience with scientific examination and analysis, including coordinating analytical work and interpreting findings to inform conservation decisions
Strong conservation documentation skills, including written and photographic documentation and the use of relevant digital, image management, and collections database tools
Proven ability to manage complex projects, priorities, resources, budgets, and deadlines while providing leadership or mentorship to staff, interns, or volunteers
Proficiency in conducting and interpreting scientific analyses such as e.g. p-XRF and digital X-radiography
Excellent organizational, problem-solving, communication, consultation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines
Experience with conservation documentation in a digital content management system. Familiarity with TMS is an asset.
Ability to safely perform precise, physically demanding conservation work, travel with collection objects when required, and respond to urgent conservation needs outside regular working hours
WHAT WE OFFER
Comprehensive benefits coverage:
For permanent and full-time contract positions (conditions apply), enjoy paid benefits for individuals and families, a health spending account, and an Employee Assistance Program.
Worry-free retirement savings
: With our optional pension plan, you benefit from an employer-matched Defined Benefit contribution plan, which provides predictable lifetime retirement income, survivor benefits, and early retirement options without the stress of investment decisions.
Perks:
Free ROM membership for permanent full-time and part-time staff, plus discounts to over 200 attractions through Attractions Ontario.
And more!

Reporting to the SVP, Commercial Enterprises, this role oversees retail sales, customer service, merchandise buying, name-drop product development, Shopify and e-commerce operations.
As a key leader within Commercial Enterprises, you will drive revenue growth, optimize operational performance, and deliver exceptional retail experiences that connect visitors and non-visitor shoppers with ROM's exhibitions, collections, and brand. You will lead a team responsible for front-of-house and back-of-house retail operations while fostering strong relationships with artists, suppliers, manufacturers, and internal stakeholders.

Take a hands-on approach to lead and inspire a high-performing retail team responsible for in-store sales, customer service, merchandise buying, ecommerce operations, and retail business administration, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and exceptional service.
Drive ROM Retail's overall financial performance by monitoring sales trends, product margins, inventory performance, and key performance indicators, ensuring revenue targets are met while delivering an outstanding visitor experience.
Develop and execute retail merchandising strategies that support ROM exhibitions, galleries, public programs, and institutional priorities through thoughtfully curated product assortments and innovative retail experiences.

Collaborate with colleagues across the Museum to ensure retail programs align with institutional priorities, exhibition storytelling, digital initiatives, community engagement efforts, and brand standards.
Champion operational excellence by implementing best practices in retail operations, inventory management, procurement, financial reporting, and customer service while ensuring compliance with ROM policies and procedures.

University or college degree/diploma in Retail Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Supply Chain, Procurement, or Purchasing certifications are considered an asset.
A minimum of 5–7 years of progressive retail leadership experience, including responsibility for business operations, merchandising, inventory management, sales performance, and customer experience.
Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing teams in a fast-paced retail, e-commerce, attraction, hospitality, cultural, or customer-facing environment.
Strong financial and business acumen, with experience managing budgets, analyzing sales performance, monitoring KPIs, and driving revenue growth through data-informed decision-making.

As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost 21st-century museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values. Join our team at ROM for a rewarding opportunity as a Visitor Experience Concierge during our upcoming peak periods.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking enthusiastic
, service-oriented individuals to join ROM as a
Visitor Experience Concierge
. Reporting to the Assistant Managers of Visitor Experience and working under the guidance of the Visitor Experience Leads, this front-line position is the welcoming face of ROM. You’ll ensure a smooth, engaging, and visitor-focused experience by greeting guests, managing entry points and coat check, and offering support at membership and ticketing stations.
This role is ideal for folks who thrive in fast-paced, public environments, are passionate about delivering outstanding customer service, and enjoy making each visitor feel valued and welcome.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Greet and direct visitors while managing queues, scanning tickets, and supporting self-serve and mobile ticketing kiosks
Operate the coat check, ensuring secure and efficient handling of personal items
Assist visitors and members at the service desk with museum planning, ticketing, and memberships
Support sales and engagement by identifying cross-selling and upselling opportunities
Respond professionally and empathetically to visitor concerns and feedback
Attend training and participate in onboarding support for new team members
Assist in preparing the front-of-house areas and maintaining operational readiness throughout the day
Support wayfinding during disruptions and event setups
Perform other duties as required to ensure an exceptional visitor experience
WHAT YOU BRING
Secondary School Diploma; post-secondary education in hospitality, tourism, or customer service is an asset
Up to 1 year of experience in customer service, hospitality, or sales
Strong communication and listening skills, with oral proficiency in English (French or another second language is an asset)
A proactive, guest-centred approach to problem-solving and service delivery
Comfort working in fast-paced, high-volume public spaces
Ability to use tablets, mobile devices, POS systems, and ticketing software
Reliable and punctual, with strong attention to detail and a team-oriented attitude
Willingness to work variable shifts, including weekends, evenings, statutory holidays, and full-time hours during peak periods (e.g., December holidays, March Break, Family Day weekend)
SALARY & TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT
Start date: October 2026
Open date: August 24, 2026
Close date: September 18, 2026
Status: Part-time contract
Employee group: OPSEU Local 543
Salary: $23.74 - $27.13 per hour
Schedule: Up to 24 hours weekly
Probationary period: 420 hours or six (6) months
Location: Toronto, ON (onsite)
WHAT TO EXPECT IN OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS
Our recruitment process for the Visitor Experience Concierge opportunity will include an
Invitation-Only Hiring Event at ROM in September 2026
.
Application & initial screening
: Apply online. Selected individuals will be invited to complete a pre-recorded video questionnaire to tell us more about your interest in ROM, your customer service experience, and the impact you could make as part of our Visitor Experience team.
Invitation-Only Hiring Event
: Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to attend an in-person hiring event at the Royal Ontario Museum in September 2026. The event will provide an opportunity to meet members of the Visitor Experience and Human Resources teams, learn more about the role and working at ROM, and participate in our interview and selection activities.
Final selection
: Following the hiring event, selected candidates will be contacted regarding next steps. Candidates receiving a verbal offer will be required to successfully complete ROM's pre-employment requirements, including a background check and professional reference verification.
Please note:
The September hiring event is
by invitation only
. Due to anticipated interest in this opportunity, only candidates selected through the initial screening process will receive an invitation and event details.
The above process may change or vary based on operational requirements and the number of candidates participating.
**All virtual conversations and interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams and may be recorded.**
WHY PEOPLE CHOOSE ROM
Cultural engagement:
Daily interactions with Toronto's diverse culture and international visitors offer insights into social and cultural trends. We champion inclusive community programs and connections through diverse experiences.
Continuous learning:
At ROM, expertise and continuous skill development are paramount. Our culture of curiosity and open-mindedness fosters growth beyond traditional career paths.
Passion & fulfillment:
Our work in preserving and curating cultural narratives brings deep satisfaction. We are passionate about the arts, global history, cultural diversity, and leveraging digital technologies to enhance accessibility.
Team & culture:
ROM promotes a positive workplace with collaborative, supportive teams that encourage creativity and innovation. We value new ideas and collective problem-solving.
Academic collaboration:
We are committed to education, partnering with universities and providing student resources, underscoring our dedication to research and accessibility.
If you’re excited about this role, even if your experience differs from the specific requirements, we encourage you to apply. We’re keen to meet candidates who can contribute their talents to our goals, and will consider an equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, education, and experience.
COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, INCLUSION, & ACCESSIBILITY
At ROM, we embrace diversity in our exhibits, communities, and teams. We encourage applications from racialized persons, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQI+ individuals, and those who can further diversify our ideas. We are committed to equitable employment opportunities and a workplace free from discrimination and harassment.
We welcome and accommodate candidates with disabilities throughout the selection process. Please contact us at careers@rom.on.ca for assistance.

ROM does not require “Canadian experience.” International applicants with equivalent experience are encouraged to apply.

title: Engineer, BPV
description:

At Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA), we are deeply committed to safety and passionate about making Ontario a safer place to live, work and play. As one of Ontario’s public safety regulators, established by the provincial government, our team of more than 450 professionals administer safety regulations and enhance public safety across multiple sectors - boilers and pressure vessels and operating engineers; elevating devices, amusement devices and ski lifts; and fuels. Our people are our greatest asset and every role is vital to our vision of working together for safer communities —today and tomorrow.
Position Summary:
Engineer employees are represented by The Society of United Professionals, IFPTE Local 160. As an Engineer, BPV, you will assess the safety of submissions from the clients for the registration or variance to the design of pressure retaining components and systems such as boilers, pressure vessels, piping and fittings in accordance with the provincial act, regulations and adapted codes and standards.
Job Responsibilities:
Evaluate design submissions in relation to the Ontario Regulations and adapted codes and standards (CSA, ASME and ANSI) including:
Review TSSA application forms and confirm manufacturer’s qualifications such as an approved QC program
Analyze component or system’s technical drawings and calculations including performing stress calculations
Follow up with client to address outstanding information requirements or technical issues
Present and review submission with internal committees where necessary (e.g. variances)
Extend approval through issuing of CRN (Canadian Registration Number) when appropriate
Respond to client requests for consultation regarding the regulations, codes and standards
Research changes to codes + standards and share with TSSA colleagues such as other Engineers, Inspectors and Technical Specialists
Provide technical support to field staff as requested
Contribute to the creation and maintenance of internal process documentation such as SOP’s (Standard Operating Procedures) and external documents such as guidelines for industry
Actively participate in promoting public safety as a member of CSA/or ASME committees
Participate in audits of clients to ensure compliance with regulations, codes and standards
Continuously develop knowledge of components and systems design as well as applicable regulatory documentation
Job Qualifications:
Mechanical engineering degree from a Canadian university or other academic program that is recognized by the Professional Engineers of Ontario (PEO) for licensure.
P.Eng. license
3-5 years of engineering experience in a related pressure equipment industry.
Candidates with the following qualifications are preferred:
Sound knowledge of boiler and pressure vessel designs
Knowledge of the Ontario Acts, Regulations, and safety codes (CSA and ASME)
Software application proficiency in Microsoft Office, PV Elite, Turbo IX and SolidWorks
Working knowledge of welding techniques and associated metallurgy and materials

At TSSA, your impact is helping create a safer Ontario. As a Fuels Engineer, you'll work closely with customers and colleagues to support understanding safety requirements and promote compliance. Evaluate Compliance of Fuel Systems and Devices:
Review engineering submissions, applications, technical drawings, calculations, and supporting documentation to assess compliance with applicable legislation, regulations, and adopted codes and standards.

: Complete technical assessments and issue approvals, variances, registrations, and other regulatory authorizations following technical review and assessment of fuel systems, appliances, and equipment.

Apply experience working with engineering quality management systems, engineering review processes, and electronic records management practices. Demonstrate the ability to evaluate complex technical issues and identify safety risk.

Review incident, inspection, and operational data to identify trends, emerging risks, and key risk drivers.

Collaborate Across Teams:
Partner with Operations, Data Analytics, and other stakeholders to strengthen risk-informed decision-making and enhance analytical tools.

title: Grants and Programs Committee Member (Volunteer)
description:
Join TAF's Grants and Programs Committee
Help Advance Climate Action in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area
The Atmospheric Fund (
TAF
) is seeking new members for its Grants and Programs Committee.
This committee plays an important role in advancing climate action across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area by reviewing funding proposals, making recommendations on funding for grants and programs that help reduce carbon emissions and support healthy, resilient communities, and providing staff with insights regarding trends, needs and opportunities for supporting climate action.
About TAF
TAF is a regional climate agency that invests in low-carbon solutions for the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area (GTHA) and helps scale them up for broad implementation. We are experienced leaders and collaborate with stakeholders in the private, public and non-profit sectors who have ideas and opportunities for reducing carbon emissions. We advance the most promising concepts by investing, providing grants, influencing policies and running programs. We’re particularly interested in ideas that offer benefits beyond carbon reduction such as improving people’s health, creating new jobs, boosting urban resiliency, and contributing to a fairer society. TAF is a proud member of the
Low Carbon Cities Canada (LC3) network
.
For the GTHA to be carbon neutral by 2050, much needs to be done, and quickly. TAF is focused on enabling the acceleration and scale-up of low-carbon solutions to reach that goal.
About the Grants and Programs Committee
The
Grants and Programs Committee
is a standing committee appointed by TAF's Board of Directors. The committee supports the Board by:
Reviewing grant and program funding proposals
Making recommendations on funding approvals and conditions
Providing strategic advice on grants and program priorities and opportunities
Supporting oversight of funded activities
Providing input to support effective program implementation
An opportunity to contribute to climate solutions
We're looking for several new members to join the Grants and Programs Committee for terms beginning in 2027.
We're particularly interested in individuals with significant professional experience (typically 5 to 10+ years) in climate solutions and related fields, including expertise in designing, funding, implementing, or scaling impactful initiatives. We welcome applications from people with a range of backgrounds and experiences, including those with expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Electric vehicles, public and active transportation
Electricity sector decarbonization
Buildings, energy efficiency, and retrofits
Market transformation and scaling solutions
Program design, delivery, and evaluation
Grantmaking and strategic funding
Finance, investment, and capital mobilization
Community engagement, community benefits, social equity, and social innovation
No one candidate is expected to bring expertise in every area. Strong committees are built on diverse perspectives and expertise, and we welcome applicants who can contribute both.
Members join a thoughtful and collaborative group of leaders and experts from across the climate sector and related fields. The committee offers a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful climate action while learning from and connecting with peers who bring a wide range of experiences and perspectives.
Time Commitment
The committee meets three times per year, with meetings typically lasting about three hours. Meetings are hybrid, and members are encouraged to attend in person if feasible. Meetings are scheduled on weekdays during business hours.
Committee members should expect to spend time reviewing meeting materials in advance. Package length varies depending on the agenda and funding proposals under consideration, and preparation time may range from a few hours to more significant review for some meetings. TAF staff prepare and distribute meeting materials, manage the grant review process, facilitate meetings, and are available support committee members as needed.
Application Process
We're using TAF's recruitment platform to support an efficient, accessible, and equitable selection process for committee appointments.
"Start your application" at the top right of this page; you'll submit your résumé and answer a short about your interest in serving on the committee and the experience, expertise, and perspectives you would bring. Your responses to these questions will be reviewed without identifying information so that reviewers can focus on your interests, experience, and perspectives. You'll also be asked a few brief administrative questions and will have the option to complete a confidential demographic survey, which is collected separately from applications and not shared with reviewers.
We encourage you to answer the questions in your own words. We're interested in hearing about your experience and perspective, not a perfect application.
Applications will be accepted until September 30, 2026. We will begin a rolling review of applications on September 21, 2026, and encourage interested candidates to apply early.
Shortlisted candidates will be invited to meet with senior TAF staff and the Committee Chair. Recommendations for appointment by to TAF's Board of Directors will be presented at the November 3, 2026 meeting; names are kept confidential until appointed. All applicants will be notified once the recruitment process is complete.

Position Purpose:
The Postdoctoral Fellow, Wildlife Science is responsible for planning, organizing, and implementing investigative research and communication related to a defined research project in a subject of interest to the TZ Science Teams (Reproductive, Veterinary, Welfare, Nutrition, and Species Recovery Sciences). This position will assist and provide support in implementing the Strategic Plan.
Scope of Work:
The Toronto Zoo invites applications for a post-doctoral fellow interested in a dedicated research project to assist the Zoo in developing an ethical framework for Indigenous partnerships as part of the governance framework for the National Wildlife Cryobank.
The post-doctoral fellow will work closely with the Zoo’s Director of Indigenous Relations, Chief Science Officer and other staff as needed. The fellow will also be informally supported by an experienced inter-disciplinary circle of project-affiliated supervisors outside the Zoo who will provide additional intellectual/academic guidance and general research support as may be required through the post-doctoral fellowship experience.
Research Focus:
Given the transdisciplinary and public -facing nature of this initiative, the post-doctoral fellow is expected to have exceptional research and communication skills. Their capacity to undertake planning, organizing, implementing and sharing investigative research that spans a range of disciplines, potentially including Indigenous studies, Indigenous law, Indigenous governance and co-governance arrangements; data sovereignty; applied intercultural ethics; wildlife conservation; and cryobanking will be invaluable. Curiosity and ability to listen, learn and adjust within a fluid multidisciplinary environment will be an asset.
Expectations from this post-doctoral fellowship include in-depth research, a jurisdictional scan, exploration and development of an Indigenous engagement strategy, potential governance models including data sovereignty, access and benefit sharing principles, and considerations of intellectual property rights relating to Indigenous knowledge systems in the context of conservation cryobanking.
The research will provide key inputs into the National Wildlife Cryobank’s governance framework, which will consider the following elements:
Foundational values and principles in establishing ethical relationships and partnerships with First Nations and Indigenous communities.
Approaches and protocols for engaging First Nations and Indigenous communities in the National Wildlife Cryobank Project.
Indigenous representation and integration of Indigenous knowledge systems in the cryobank’s governance framework.
Considerations for data sovereignty of stored samples, including the application of OCAP™ principles and the CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance.
Guidelines for Access and Benefit Sharing Agreements, in compliance with the Nagoya Protocol and any existing Indigenous-led initiatives or models.
Preference will be given to qualified First Nations, Inuit or Metis candidates or candidates with verifiable direct experience conducting Indigenous-related research and working closely and respectfully with Indigenous communities.
Core Role Responsibilities:
Oversight of a defined research project, including grant writing, experimental design, data collection, partner communication, student training, and related tasks.
Oversees grant/donor funding reports and ensures proper use of financial resources to carry out research investigations.
Liaises with Indigenous communities, governments and organizations, and Wildlife Science teams as required to implement research project objectives.
Develops and strengthens existing liaisons with Indigenous communities and organizations, academic, governmental and similar organizations as related to the research project.
Supervises and/or oversees training of students assigned to the same project, including graduate and undergraduate students.
Communicates results of research project to Indigenous communities, governments and organizations, Zoo staff, volunteers, and the public, and interacts with the media as a subject matter resource as needed.
Publishes research data in academic journals and conference proceedings.
Provides updates of activities for board and annual reports.
Actively seeks external funding for research project, in consultation with Toronto Zoo Wildlife Conservancy staff, as appropriate.
Technical Knowledge and Skills:
Must possess a PhD (preferably no more than 2 years post-graduation) from a recognized institution in one of the following disciplines: Indigenous studies, Indigenous law, Indigenous governance and co-governance arrangements; data sovereignty; applied intercultural ethics.
Specific interest and research experience with applying one of these disciplines to wildlife conservation and/or conservation cryobanking is an asset.
Curiosity and ability to listen, learn and adjust within a fluid multidisciplinary environment will be an asset.
Must have research experience with techniques related to the Science Team functions.
Must have demonstrated ability to publish results in peer reviewed journals and obtain external funding.

We’re here to help. When an injury or illness happens on the job, we move quickly to provide wage-loss benefits, medical coverage and support to help people get back to work. This is a temporary (12 month) position.
As the IT Portfolio Manager - Financial Analysis, you will play a key role in helping WSIB maximize the value of its technology investments. You will provide advisory support across all aspects of the IT portfolio, ensuring projects are effectively governed, financially managed, and aligned with strategic business objectives. By leveraging financial analysis, business case development, benefits realization, and portfolio governance practices, you will help drive informed decision-making, operational efficiency, and continuous improvement across the IT organization. Working closely with area leaders and stakeholders, you will support the evaluation and prioritization of technology investments, ensuring initiatives deliver measurable business outcomes and contribute to WSIB's long-term strategic goals.
On a practical level, you would:
Provide financial analysis and management recommendations, helping to demonstrate the value of IT investments and support investment approval decisions.
Conduct in-depth analysis to influence senior leadership and drive data-driven, evidence-based decisions within IT.
Collaborate with industry leaders (e.g., Gartner and Forrester) to develop organizational best practices that support optimal business outcomes.
Perform cost-benefit analyses and ROI assessments to evaluate project feasibility.
Support business planning by developing effective prioritization frameworks based on KPIs and benefits realization tracking.
Assist with financial forecasting, reporting, budgeting, and financial analysis using Microsoft Office applications, including Project, advanced Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint.
Major Responsibilities:
IT portfolio advisor for oversight on governance, risk management, reporting, communication strategies, including, but not limited to:
Guiding portfolio through development and maturity phases;
Benchmarking dependencies within assigned portfolios related to IT roadmap;
Coordinating with internal teams for portfolio health check assessments;
Developing portfolio managed protocols;
Engaging stakeholders within dependent disciplines, such as; Contract Management, Quality Management, Procurement, and Legal;
Championing innovative and value-add solutions for portfolio deliverables;
Developing communication vehicles for executive management teams including risk assessment, dependencies, corporate goal alignment and budget
Assess IT portfolio viability within appropriate timelines and interdependencies, including, but not limited to:
Assessing initiative proposals and business cases;
Advising on requirement gathering consolidations
Creating executive management reports for portfolio risks, budget, monthly status, recommendations, health checks;
Designing and managing communication plans and strategies;
Managing standard change management practices;
Monitoring and advising on portfolio health check assessments;
Contribute to the development of portfolio artifacts for terms of reference, concept documents, business cases, including, but not limited to:
Promoting integrity of portfolio processes with the PMO;
Advising PMO statuses, as required;
Recommending changes and improvements to portfolio processes and methodologies.
Facilitate the IT intake process including:
Facilitating meetings for new requests
Forecasting resources
Developing and supporting reporting and monitoring tools.
Support Manager, Planning Management:
Providing advice and guidance for portfolio governance and benefits realization;
Ensuring support protocols and appropriate standards and best practices;
Advising on portfolio interrelationships supporting priority and resource allocation decisions;
Promoting continuous improvement through lessons learned and facilitating recommendations.
Implement project portfolio dashboards, scorecards and reports:
Creation and generation of IT scorecards;
Providing recommendations for dashboards, scorecard reporting;
Planning for the 3-to-5 years ahead, consistent with the IT roadmap.
Proving advice on IT initiatives that are of a sensitive nature (for example, IT outsourcing) as assigned:
Ensuring adherence to processes and governance in terms of time, cost and benefits;
Managing end-to-end portfolio scope, resources, budget and deliverables;
Facilitating and managing meetings.
What You'll Bring:
We're looking for a strategic and analytical professional who can combine financial expertise, portfolio management knowledge, and stakeholder collaboration to drive informed technology investment decisions.
8 to 10 years of progressive experience in portfolio management, financial analysis, business case development, project management, or a related discipline.
CPA designation is a strong asset.
A university degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Information Technology, or a related field
Experience supporting large, complex projects or portfolios within a technology or business environment.
Strong analytical, financial modelling, reporting, and stakeholder management capabilities.
The ability to translate complex data into meaningful insights and recommendations for senior leaders.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent is an asset.
Experience with portfolio governance, benefits realization, business case evaluation, and technology investment management

description:

We’re here to help. When an injury or illness happens on the job, we move quickly to provide wage-loss benefits, medical coverage and support to help people get back to work.
